texts: I thought Becca Fanning did a great job with the conclusion to the Saint family. They all had their moment and it was time for the leader to have his as well. They all had their own story which was put together to create one big story line. After reading the series this one is one of my favorites. I think this conclusion left you with that feeling of complete. The people in the novella were so likeable that they all deserved their happily ever after which I felt they all received. I recieved an arc in exchange for a honest review.
Good old tetris with original music. I love it and now my kids. Good game.

I don't like taste of this aloe water, it's very artificial and over sweet. I'd prefer just to drink water with aloe gel for health purposes even if the taste would not be very good (could always use in a veggie/fruit shakes).
I'm glad I was able to try this product but thanks for unnecessary calories and the chemical sweet after taste in my throat. I won't buy!

this is a cute shower cap. It comes in a little plastic envelope with a snap making it easy to tuck in a suitcase. The teal pattern is pleasant. The cap itself is unlined and made of rather crinkly plastic. The elastic is covered with white plastic. I've been growing out my hair and it is now past my shoulders. I was pleased that this cap was able to accommodate it all. The plastic is waterproof. the cap should fit most head sizes.

I use shower caps when airbrushing makeup and when actually painting the interior of my house as well as for showers and deep conditioning. This one certainly performs as well as any. the pattern is pretty but it is not especially comfortable or well made. especially considering the price point.  It does the job it was designed to do but the quality is on a par with the dollars store or discount beauty supplier.

The price listed currently on Amazon is pretty insane, and no 8 ounce candy is worth that much unless it's gold plated.

The good - the flavors are good.  I don't think they're gross, plasticy, etc...  They taste good to me.  I like the resealable packet, and that each square is just "loose" inside, no wrappers to unwrap like normal starburst candies.  And the reds are my favorites, and my son's favorites.  So it's nice to have a whole packet of flavors we'll eat, with no colors we'd toss.

The bad - they do not taste quite like the originals.  My son still prefers the larger, original ones, but for me I actually like these smaller ones as much as the originals.  For me, they're not nearly as saliva generating as the originals for me, which is a benefit.

But if you're looking for that exact flavor and consistency as the originals, this is not the package for you.

Well written story with nice plot and story line. It was a bit confusing for me sometimes because there are a lot going on in this story. Kian is forced to be heir because his brother disappears. At a party he meets Savvy who is a waitress there. They have instant-love and attraction. They have both a lot to deal with.
There are a lot of twists and turns in this story. They confused me but gives a lot of action and drama to it.
The chemistry is okay. I would have liked there was more depth in the story instead of all the different twists.
But it is an enjoyable read.

I voluntarily read an ARC of this book for my honest review!

I am really loving this series. When Antonio and Angela are together you don't want to put this book down. It shows a different side to Antonio that I love. I am dying to finally read what Antonio is keeping from Angela. When I read the paragraph I was crushed and I am dying to know what is going to happen

This series is getting better and better. I loved Cyrus and Tara(Birdie) and the sex was hot between them. I felt for Tara and what she went thru and I got what Cyrus was doing making her strong and not need anyone but herself but when he left it was hard to read because you know they are good together. I loved the ending and can't wait to read the next book in this series

With Vivienne telling Jacob that she loves him but not hearing it back stung, but she wouldn't give him up. She knew Jacob felt more for her but couldn't say. With wanted to be with Vivienne, Jacob wanted to do so much to her in the playroom. Jacob thinks he's not romantic but he truly is and wants Vivienne to be happy. Going on a trip to Italy might have finally done a job on Jacob and letting Vivienne in, but what Jacob confesses will Vivienne leave him? Can't wait to read what happens next
I enjoyed this series but only recommend it for KU members. I wouldnt spend money on it. KU
All of us have had a crush on a famous person at one time or another.  What if your crush moved in next door? What would you do? Read and find out what Callie did.  #KindleUnlimited

KB Winters loves to write novella series. This one is written in 5 parts which was a bit long for me. I started skimming through some parts. Kat and Jace struggle through a lot of pain and heartache in their relationship. They spend more time apart than together. They do get their HEA but the ending felt a bit rushed. #KindleUnlimited

Other than Sarah Palin becoming President of the United States, I rather doubt that the world will come to an end in 2012.  Of course, I do readily concede that Palin as Prez would be enough to urge the universe to accelerate to its heat-death a few trillion years < schedule.

All of that said, there is one facet of this movie that I find to be rather fascinating.  We live in a solar system that is, for the most part, ultra-hostile to life as we know it.  To be sure, it is possible that there is microbial life beneath the icy sheath of Europa & perhaps there is microbial life on Titan ~ I get that.  However, for the post part, this cosmic backwater in the middle of Orion's Arm has little tolerance for sentient life that is advanced enough to build cities, write poetry & vote for a straight Democratic ticket.

The exception, of course, is what Carl Sagan eloquently referred to as a pale blue dot:  planet Earth.  It is here & only here that we find a celestial bastion that is overflowing with life.  The question the present movie poses, then, is this:  WHAT IF our beloved but fragile Earth began to resemble the other planets in our solar system?  It's a sobering question & it's certainly not a good thing for the human race.

Beyond that, other than some eye-candy special effects, I found this film to be rather bland.  You can only have a plane take off on a runway that is crumbling so many times before it starts to get old.  The sequence in the limo was fun, but entirely unbelievable.

I've always enjoyed movies with John Cusack & Amanda Peet.  They have a great chemistry together and they're both fine Thespians in their own rights.  For that reason alone, this flick is worth seeing.  Unfortunately, I found the ending to be a cop-out and pretty much a 21st rendition of the story of Noah's Ark.  Sad, but true.

There is a line in this movie in which the Arnie Terminator says "It is time."  I so wish that someone would have told the writers and director that BEFORE this movie came out.  That is to say, it would have been nice if they had been notified that the TERMINATOR story had run its course.
Unfortunately, that didn't happen, and T3 was made.  This movie should be used as "Exhibit A" as to what happens when a good idea is recycled one too many times.  Instead of continuing w/the excellent story of 1 & 2, this one comes off as generic, tired and rather silly.
One of the problems lies in the fact that the T-1000 from T2 didn't give the writers anywhere to "go" to make the Terminator in this one even more impressive.  So, what they come up with are some absurdly far-fetched powers that don't coincide very well with logic.
The lone bright spot of this movie is Kristanna Loken.  She is most assuredly cast perfectly as the new Terminator.  She is  drop-dead gorgeous, has a fantastic athletic body and she also has that "don't mess with me" look.  Seeing her come thru the time portal naked might just be worth the price of renting this movie - but the storyline certainly isn't.
It is sad that this movie was so bad, as T1 was a classic and T2 was even better.  All T3 does is throw in a lot of ad hoc details that un-do everything that T2 did.  Apparently the film-makers thought that the ending was going to be a big "surprise."  Anyone who half paid attention to the movie could predict what would happen 1/3 of the way in.
 Sadly, the theme of the movie is nearly as predictable as how bad it looked like it was going to be.  For all TERMINATOR fans out there, I would admonish you to watch T1 & T2 over and over again, but skip this one entirely.

The second book in this series picks immediately after the ending of book one.  This book is less of a romp as it dealt with Gustavia's family issues and her soul mate, Finn.

This book is all about resolving the past to leave room for exploring future hopes and dreams.

I liked the first book a little more than this one... a more adventurous and airy feeling in book one.  But this one drew me into Gustavia's emotional needs.

The treasure hunt was almost an afterthought to the plot.

I do like the author's writing style and the sweetness of the romance.  I did not miss the use of bad language that permeates many contemporary romance stories.

Looking forward to book three in the series.

I guess this book has taught me to read the entire description of a book be for I buy it.  I didn't do that
....and even skimming this story was painful.  It's a bunch of macho b.s. and foul language.  Oh for a zero star rating or even a negative  rating.  Do not waste your time.

Plot unrealistic and contrived and predictable.  Sex scenes okay though having the woman say s*** several times was off putting.  This was written hastily to get to the cliffhanger...I just don't care to buy more of this s***.
I have read many paranormal romances but this one did not engage me.  Just my opinion.

Maybe it was a slow start.  I did not get drawn into the characters.  Then there was there was the 'be continued'
notice listed at the end of chapters.  I see no reason to struggle to get into a book just to end in a cliff hanger.
I could not get into this story.

Carry Me Home is the third book in the Home Series and I have really enjoyed this series and the characters.  In a lot of books, you have these hard to believe scenarios on how the couple meets or some of the obstacles the have to deal with to be together and you don't get that in this book or the others.

We catch up with Riley three years later, just as she is going home for the summer after finishing her Junior year at Kansas State.  She has finally been able to move on after Jesse broke up with her.  She is enjoying college life and even has a boyfriend.  Riley and Evan have been dating for a year, and are very happy.  He has helped her start to live again.  She is heading home to Carver and he is heading to Kansas City to start his job since he just graduated.

Riley gets home and starts to get settled, starts working at the flower shop again and spending time with Mandy.  Brandon comes home from being in the Army after he was severely injured.  Not too long after Brandon comes home, Jesse shows up.  It is the first time he has been in Carver in three years since he joined the Marine Corp and Riley is shocked to run into him.  They start working on their friendship since that is how they started and something they were good at.

The story of Riley and Jesse is not over yet, even if they only remain friends.  I have been rooting for them since the first book of the series.  They have been through so much in their young lives, much more than they should have been through, but they come through stronger individually.  This is not a book to be read as a standalone and recommend you read it.

Ok, I was highly disappointed in this book.  I downloaded it and thought, This is going to be awesomethere are over 11,000 pages in this book!  WRONG, it only took up 33% of the download.  A different book took up the rest.

So, Marie is the most nave Mafia princess ever!  She has no clue how the family actually operates, other than she knows everything is about the family.  Roman is the man she is promised to, Alek is his brother.  While Roman is actually very intelligent, he comes across as all brawn and no brain.  Not so, he just doesnt say anything, unless its needed.  Alek comes across as a sleaze.  I don't really feel that was the authors intentions, but thats what I got from it.

The writing is mediocre; intimate scenes are hot, but the remainder leaves a lot to be desired.  I was hoping this would be a good Mafia romance, but I struck out on this one.  Doubt I will read more of Ms. Watsons work.

Let me start by saying, this COULD be a 5 star book very easily. It WAS a 5 star, until about the last 2 or 3 chapters. The storyline is very good. Jo, or Joanna, is a niece in the mob. She agrees to pay her father's debt by working for the enemy family. Meet, Greyson, the heir to said family. He's a habitual playboy, wants nothing to do with love or the 'Family', but knows he can't turn his back on it.
As I said, the storyline is really good, if not a new one, but I had extreme issues with the ending. It builds you up, just waiting for some climatic event, but that really never comes. It's almost as if the author was rushed, got tired of writing, or couldn't find a better way to finish. What I expected to be 5 or 6 more chapters, to finish the story, ends in 2 or 3 pages. I was left with a feeling of 'was that the end'? Not saying don't read it, someone else may truly love the book, but I felt it was not complete. I will say that I'm not giving up on Ms. Song. I think she has great potential to become an excellent author and I hope she does. The writing was good, editing was decent and the passion for writing is there. Just needs a little more focus.

Ugh, stalkerish much? This book reads like a bad script of the classic stalker. The H gets off on her house, breaks in, lays in her bed, sniffs her clothing and uses her lotion. That's just plain creepy! I couldn't respect the so-called badass h, because she found that behavior sexy. Come on! Any sane woman would be putting a bullet in him, or calling the police, at the least. He was written to be a dominant alpha, but his behavior was the exact opposite. More like an insecure little boy. And the language. Jeez, during intimate moments, his dialog reminded me of 15 yr old boys
The writing...the author desperately needs to research MCs. First, this woman should never be in a MC. Right off the bat she lets her emotions override her actions. She's telling secrets that could get her and the club in trouble. Things she could be killed for. Now, I'm all for equal rights, but I want my MC books to be about hard core, aloha men, with a strong lady. She was not! I wanted to shoot her myself.
I certainly wouldn't recommend this book.
The story was a fun read. However, the heroine drove me crazy at times. She was so insecure and needy. Having said that, she was quite inventive as well.

Using the high yield ink was a new experience for me; however, I am so glad that I discovered this.  You see, I was printing 1500 pages for my newest project.  HP ink has never disappointed me and this just made me realize anew why I like it so much.  I got almost 800 pages printed out of each cartridge.  The black is clear, true from the first page to the 800th.  I cannot commend this product too highly.  Just get the high yield and print as much as you need to do.  You will not be disappointed!

While I am a reader of the McCandless works, I found this little novella to be unnecessary.  I agree with the author's suggestion that any reader of this novella should read the Novel first.  I cannot imagine this work making any sense unless that suggestion is followed.  But, to continue thinking about this one, everything is too predictable!  From the first words to the last words, the reader knows what is going to happen.  The characters are almost wooden as they go about this action adventure.  One cannot imagine so much blood being shed in such a brief moment and the disaster to the ballroom and the gowns of the wedding party.  Too much!

The promised flashing red LED was not present in the camera, and no obvious way to add one. However, this does mean that the camera is totally waterproof!

Even without the LED its a good deterrent, but the LED would really help.
Easy to install - weighs next to nothing, you could install it with double sided sticky foam, no wires to run, its adjustable. It's pretty good.

This is bulky, not for quickly securing your laptop whilst you get a coffee. But if you are working a tradeshow stand, or using your laptop in a store display, this will secure it down perfectly.

I suspect you *could* break it, but its very strong, and doing so would probably destroy your device. Small comfort, but hopefully the  would-be thief will see that and give up before harm is done.

What this really is, it cheap insurance. When you look at the cost of your MacBook, or any other small laptop you are securing with this, its a bargain.

She was a free spirited kind of gal.
 He was a straight-laced kind of man.
They both got on each others nerves, but the attraction towards each other was the dynamite..if only she took things seriously and he would ease up on the reins.

Could this disaster ending up a happy ever after?

I absolutely loved this story! Mia is a loving artist whos pretty laid back when it comes to tough situations and Michael is the complete opposite with his business suits and serious aura. These two are complete opposites, but as we know and hear all the timeopposites attract. At the beginning you can tell that this relationship is going to go off with a bang because these two ooze sexual tension.

The banter and light moments were great. The pace was nice and easy to follow along with what was going on. 

Easy and highly enjoyed read. 

~Tempting Sexy Thoughts

I love the connotative meanings that go along with the title of Quinn and Tazens story, Hard to Break, because there are a multitude of positive and negative experiences that they go through both individually and as a couple that definitely demonstrate what it means to splinter, fracture, and come unhinged.

Since her mothers death, Quinns life has been like fighting an uphill battle that always sends her tumbling down, but that hasn't stopped her from trying to move forward, relying on only herself to keep a roof over her and her father and keep the shop open and out of the red. All of these are daunting tasks, but through it all, Quinn refuses to break; she refuses to quit, and one way or another, shes going to prove that the garage is where she belongs no matter what the cocky son of b***h says!

Tazen Watts - the name oozes sex and charm - too bad none of his smooth talking wins Quinn over; in fact, his demeanor and attitude grates her nerves and turns her crush on him into an all out war of barbs and antics.

The volatile nature of Taz and Quinns relationship goes from bad to worse when Taz takes the one thing Quinns always had, threatening to unhinge her entire life and forcing her to fight dirty in order to maintain some sense of what defines her. But when everything plays out, who will break whom and what kind of fracturing will it be? The kind that draws people together or tears them even further apart?

Even though Hard to Break is a slightly predictable enemies to lovers story, I still enjoyed watching Tazen and Quinn rev each other up until they both blew in a variety of ways! I love the fact that Quinn is a phenomenal mechanic and lets her work speak for itself. Shes exactly who she portrays herself to be and to me, thats why Taz is drawn to her even though they come from completely different worlds. Taz is also quite surprising once Quinn gets underneath his tough exterior; hes actually quite sweet and knows what Quinn needs as their relationship progresses. Theres some angst but not an excessive amount. The primary focus is more on Quinns refusal to stop fighting and how Tazens realizes her unbreakable spirit is exactly why hes falling for her.

A complimentary copy was provided by the author/publisher in exchange for an honest review.

3.5 poison apples

Both Sarah and Ari epitomize the definition of a trainwreck, but their reasons for being completely unhinged drastically differ. Sarah's struggles revolve solely around her need for money in order to care for her cancer stricken mother while Ari's upheaval stems from the actions of others and the mental and physical trauma that he and those closest to him have suffered due to those people's mistreatment.

Despite their contrasting lives, Sarah and Ari form a connection from one sensual encounter on a train, and while Ari treats Sarah, at times, as nothing more than a toy...a sexual plaything, Sarah can't help but be seduced by the blond, blue-eyed Adonis, even if it means following his rules and feeling used far more than feeling cherished.

I have to admit...I had a hard time with Sarah and Ari's choices at the beginning of the story and how Sarah allowed herself to be treated by him. I completely get Ari's hesitancy and fear of commitment, but that doesn't mean he has the right to handle things the way he does. I wanted to throttle him on more than one occasion as well as shake Sarah into seeing how unhealthy her new "relationship" with Ari is. Sarah has enough to deal with when it comes to her job and her mother, so to willingly give herself to a man who treats her more like something than someone didn't sit right with me.

But because readers are given Ari's point of view, I was able to understand how truly damaged he is, which helped put things in perspective a bit more and then witnessing his interaction with Ben allowed me to see the gentler side of Ari and the reasons behind his abrupt behavior.

With the cliffhanger at the end of book 1, it will be interesting to see how Sarah and Ari move forward and what others' interference will do to any chance they have of building anything beyond a sexual relationship.

A complimentary copy was provided in exchange for an honest review.

4 Poison Apples

Henry Richardson Big Man has always been the man behind the scenes, the man on the sidelines, the man every member of Shaft and their family rely on. Readers have caught small glimpses of what makes Henry who he is, but he still remained the elusive, sunglass wearing man who hides behind his dark lenses and allows no one close enough to truly understand his past because in his mind if no one gets in then no one gets hurtits just unclear what happened to him and what its going to take to break through Henrys wall and allow him to live for himself and take his shot at happiness like all of the other members of the Shaft family have.

Rae Sloan just might be the woman to give Henry what he deserves, but theyll both have to work through their scarred pasts in order for anything to happen. Raes the perfect addition to the Shaft crew; she meshes well with the women, and she gives as good as she gets from the testosterone fueled males. Henry doesnt scare Rae; in fact, his abrasiveness pisses her off, and she isn't afraid to cut through the bulls*** and give Henry the real her and force him to be honest about who he is.

I really loved getting the Big Mans story; I wanted Henrys back story and the reasons he is who he is and I got that as well as an in-depth look at the real Henry  the dirty talking alpha male who is a fierce protector and lover. Theres still more to understand about Henry, though, because hes not quite an open book yet, so I hope that Cat Mason adds to Henry and Raes story and gives readers everything that makes Henry the Big Man.

A complimentary copy was provided in exchange for an honest review.

4 poison apples

I wasn't the biggest fan of this book. I seem to have a love/hate relationship with this authors' work. While I loved the last book in this series I really didn't like this one. I wasn't the biggest fan of either the hero or the heroine or their relationship with one another. I found myself rolling my eyes at some of their antics more often than not. Both are immature and I never really got a sense that they were meant to be. I also found parts of the story highly unlucky. Please tell me how two people who haven't had sex with anyone in eight years are suddenly masters in the bedroom. I just don't buy it.

A quick, easy and enjoyable read. Good mix of romance and mystery with a sexy dash of steaminess. All the characters were well developed - no real surprises but I didn't mind. The secondary plots added good depth to the primary story and I would definitely read more about the Whedon brothers.
Funny cozy mystery with a touch of quirk. Great interaction between the characters and a few twists to follow to the end

The Omega Paw self -cleaning cat box works great!!I LOVE IT !!!! It is much easier than scooping. My 2nd  littermaid catbox broke and I wanted to try this rather than wasting another  $120.00. This catbox does exactly what it says it will do. I had no trouble putting it together, but I can see how you might have latch trouble if it is not lined up correctly. You just roll it to the right and then to the left and empty the drawer. It doesn't get much easier than this !!  I've had no problems and I would recommend it.

Sam and Blair have been in a relationship for ages, Blair is always Sams first stop when on leave from Seal training, but after this visit nothing will be the same for either of them. I understand Blair's desperation in trying to sway Sam while he is on leave even though it is really selfish. Sam doesn't know whats really going on as neither he nor Blair appear to have really every talked about their relationship and then he has Eli  telling him whats best. Will Sam finally get his trident after wanting it since he was 16 and will Blair finally have her happy ever after??

I was given a complimentary copy of this book in exchange for an honest review.

I love cozy mysteries and this has some good points but also some bad points, I really liked the idea of Narel having an accident and getting a make over out of it but the whole can't gain weight and only eating chocolate all the time really got me. I did however like all the characters and the whole killing of "The Populars" was great and did leave me wondering who was doing it. This book has left me on the fence of reading more from Morgana Best but I think due to the great characters I will give another book a go.

I received a free copy of this book via Booksprout and am voluntarily leaving a review.

New author to me but I could not put it down!  Excellent story line great characters and I could almost feel the sweltering heat!
Loved the book.
Love it!  I really enjoyed this book and how the characters are developing!
Awesome! Loved the chemistry and love!
I am so hot right now I need to go take a cold shower! I love the relationship between Oriana and all her men because they are just so yummy!

This was a great book. It held my interest throughout. The author did a great job of making the characters so interesting and you felt like you were right there. I would recommend it. No sexual scenes so that was another plus.
different... I wasn't too sure about it at first. It was ok...
Good book. I would like to read the next book.

This is the continuation of Lacy and Drannon story, will they be able to pull of the wedding of their dreams, or will life get in the way. Although mother nature forced them to elope, Lacy still feels that a big celebration is what the family needs after near disaster.  Brillant and witty, we finally get to meet Lacy's dad and the relationship that has developed,  as well as get a glimpse into the some of the other foster kids that were impacted by Abe and Sera. Such a beautiful continuation of the series

I received a copy from the author in exchange for my honest review.

Brax and Nicole attended the same high school but walked in different circles, they only had one night.  Now 15 years later Nicole's brother is in trouble and she turns to Brax for help. Will they be able to pick up where they left off or will it all be water under the bridge. I loved this book, the lenghts in which Nicole goes to protect her brother, but it also shows her strength and fortitude. Brax oh my protective much, I wanted to smack him a couple times, but I  understand where he was coming from. I would have liked to know more about Jase a minor character,  hope he gets his  own book. This book will reel you in from the first word to the last

I received this book from the author in exchange for an honest review.  Brilliantly written, captivating  Bess is the head of her department that places kids with foster families,  Sawyer is the new president of the great wolves mc. Sparks fly whenever they meet but Bess keeps denying it until Sawyer goes to her for help when he finds a teen hiding behind his warehouse.  This book brought to mind all those missing teens that we hear about on tv, emotional riviting.  This is a must read, sometimes you have to go outside of the law to get things done. Can't wait for the next book in the series
This was my first Vampire Romance and I am hooked. Will be reading many more. Cynthia Eden's books are a must read!

This book has it all. Romance, sex, suspense, and humor make this an outstanding read. Every character is unique and interesting. The format of the book is a series of emails telling the story. I enjoyed it. The emails are interactions between Coco and her various relatives and acquaintances, bringing the reader into the loop. Great job.
I like that the couple has been in love forever and its,not another meet and fall in love book. Low on romance High angst but a good read.
I expected so much more for this book based off the others I've read. It felt scattered and forced and there just wasn't much of a story to it.
First I have to say something is in the water that the band drinks with all the opps happening. The guys,are amazing and make the stories fantastic. I couldn't put the books down.

This story is about Rylan/Evan being a college student half the time, and a sex model the other time. She tries to keep her job a secret from everyone in her life including the people she goes to school with.

But things change when one of her peers from school starts modeling with her. That's not the only issue though he's also beautiful and has a girlfriend. So it makes Rylan feel pretty crappy having to pose with him, and getting strange feelings for him.

This book has a good story line. I just couldn't get into Dallas' character. I really thought he was frustrating most of the time, unless he was doing a shoot then I thought he was awesome. The overall book is just okay. Dallas really bothered me. But it ended good, no cliffhanger, and I was happy with the results so overall it was an okay read for a short book.

This story begins when Rosabel decides to leave the Pride she's lived with for most of her life. She's tired of being the only wolf among them, and tired of fighting for her life everyday. Something brings her to Mount Roxby, and on her first night there meeting the Pack Alpha things start to change for. After meeting Theo, and feeling things she's never felt before, she must soon help them prevent a war between werewolves and vampires before it is all too late!

This book was okay. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't really great either. I liked the relationship between Theo and Rosabel! I also loved that she was very brave, and not afraid of things. What I didn't like was her stupidity sometimes, especially when it came to dating certain men.. Anyways, other then that it was a quick interesting read to pass the time with!

I liked this book but she spent to much time talking about nothing. There were a few laughs but not many but I did not figure out the killer. I did skip pages just bc it was talking about nothing interesting.  This book has a lot  of potential though. Just was not what I was looking for though.
I enjoyed this book about. It moved at a real good pace and has plenty of action. All areas were covered and it was really easy to read.

The premise of this book was great.  I haven't read another book like it!  I was intrigued after reading the description and wanted to learn more.  Loved the story, and I liked the main character, Monroe, and how she grew during the story.

This story was so good. We meet Rachel on a day that is supposed to be about her only to have it ruined by her boyfriend. She meets someone who does right by here and gets her to show her talents. She ends up having great night that comes to a halt the next day. I need to read the next part soon.

4.5 stars.  An Amazon 4 star Review means I like it, really liked it.

David Cavello is an attractive, larger than life, alpha male with the need for control in his life.  He is a college student, army  veteran is drowning in memories of death, including the death of his friend in Iraq.  He is now haunted by PTSD with flashbacks occurring both while awake and during his sleep.  As a result he rarely, almost never, brings a woman home and absolutely isn't interested in a relationship..until

Maygen is the only child to her very wealthy father, having lost her mother at the age if 12.  Her father , a very recognizable and successful  business man in the PR does everything possible to protect her.  The need for that protection becomes very clear as you read this story.  As a high fashion assistant to Dax, a very famous and movie star gorgeous fashion designer,  Maygen is as independent as possible with such a domineering father.

This is the story of a collision of the body and heart with some suspense, intrigue mixed in.  Davids PTSD and how this shapes his emotions and behavior plays a key role in the journey to happy.  Trust and need are also driving forces in this engaging story.

This is my first read by this author and thank you to NetGalley for the recommendation.  This is the third book in a series and although I have not read the prior two books, that did not in any way detract from my appreciation of this beautiful love story.

This could have made a wonderful longer story.  I so wanted to see what Fell did working with Mary.  I felt left up in the air, with the sex scene being almost longer than any thing else.  I really would have enjoyed better development of what began as a really good story idea.  As it is, the author seems to be writing to just turn short stories out.

While I'm not into explicit sexual scenes, there are only a couple and I was able to skip over them without losing the enjoyment of the story which was a fun read.  Watching this couple fall in love, yet neither knew they were actually engaged to one another.  It makes for an interesting concept and enjoyable to follow as Cherry becomes the governess of Skye' s siblings, running away from a marriage she doesn't want and falling in love, unknowingly, with the very man she has been promised to.

Talk about a tear jerker.  Aryl was the mediater between Jon and Caleb.  He was the idea man whose mind constantly turned, searching for opportunity while Jon did the numbers and managed and Caleb provided the muscle and manual organization.  Still it was Aryl who quietly was the center and backbone of the three, although it seemed on the surface that Jon was.  Now the dynamics will have to change.  It will be interesting in future series books to see how they fall, but seeing how the families continue to adjust and survive the loss of their fortunes through 1930-1931 is very real and interesting.  Great, great series, and this book is every bit as good as the first, 1929.

I was reading this book while listening to more of the problems going on in Washington and a man falling out of a plane.  There was all kinds of news to be depressed about and then I was reading this book and found some really nice people - Fiona getting through the loss of her parents but still putting one foot in front of the other because that's what you do, or you lay down and die, too.  Then there is Gray who is just a really nice guy - dependable and kind.  The kind of guy you hope your sons will grow up to be.  There are students I saw in my own classrooms and miss now that I no longer teach.  This book just had so much to relate to.  There were times there were challenges, but life has pain and in the end, there was happiness and you knew there would be.  So the bad news on the telly was easier to put on the back burner for at least a while.

Haunted Chemistry by Lindsey R. Loucks

Alexis has laundry to do in her new apartment building. She's not comfortable going down to the buildings basement but the task needs to be done. She runs into Ian, her former chemistry partner, and even though he stood her up for a date, she's glad of the company because she's a little scared of the basement. A cabinet door seems to open by itself. Back in her own apartment with Ian, her cat is acting strangely now too. The cat is staring and hissing at an open cabinet door. Alexis is sure that door wasn't open when she left to start the laundry.

Remember that old saying "don't go down to the basement"?
Alexis and Ian see a ghost and identify it very quickly. And they confront the ghost. Brave or stupid? They are pretty blas about the whole situation which I found unbelievable. Really? You just accept and go after the ghost?
This novella is written in the present tense which I have a difficult time with. Perhaps that's why I found this one difficult get into.

The premise sounded interesting for this story -- That of a young man, Joshua,  coming home for his cousin's wedding.  He's been on the outs with his father and was encouraged to make amends.  Soon the news comes out that Joshua's father had died a year ago and Joshua, the only child, was never told.  Why his 'close' family assumed he knew is anyone's guess.  They couldn't even say they left messages or tried to contact him.  After a year has gone by Joshua is left to his regrets and loss and really has to do it on his own.  Everyone else is over the mourning.

Ezra is portrayed as this playboy that pays for sex on demand.  New boy, new room, get it on, and kick them out.  He is not a likeable character and that never changed for me.  From his actions and the way the story was written, I felt he did take advantage of an old man, and swindled Joshua's inheritance.  Part of that is not knowing Ezra's background, his schooling, or very little of his acting as a CEO of a company.  All we see are his sexual acts and of course Joshua walks in on him a few times.  Of all things Joshua never remarks on those situations and how it affects their relationship. Joshua never questions if Ezra can be faithful.  You would think that he would.

I ended up skipping a lot of this story.  I was waiting for the details on the reveal and then the unveiling.  What actually happened a year ago?  How is Joshua stepping up?  As the story progresses Joshua always had a lot on his mind and major decisions to make.  But at the same time he was turning into this wishy washy whiney individual that sought answers in a bottle and was listening to everyone but his own conscience.  Sorry, I don't like my main characters to morph into these weak willed wimps.  Now maybe he's just depressed and can't handle life -- Again -- That segment colored how I felt about Josh as a character and he never redeemed himself.

This is a gay for you (GFY) contemporary story.  The setting is London and the push is that love and relationships are more important for happiness than a boat load of money.  Well, Ezra and Joshua get them both and I'd say Joshua's father got the last laugh.  - Dan's Wife

With almost 700 reviews already on this movie, I have little to add. But it does what so few modern movies do -- engages both the viewer's intellect and feelings. The way it is constructed is brilliantly clever but all the tricks and technical marvels are really in service of a touching love story -- and the idea that love can survive even our technological society -- even the loss of memory.

This documentary recounts how French high wire walker Philippe Petit and a small band of accomplices managed to string a cable across the roofs of the twin towers of the World Trade Center in 1974 so he could walk, dance, kneel, run and lie down in mid-air for an unforgettable 45 minutes.
The movie never mentions the 2001 attack that destroyed the towers but that is always in your mind and gives the movie some additional poignancy.
We meet Petit, who is articulate and almost laughably French. He had already walked on a wire between the two spires of Notre Dame in Paris and on a bridge in Sydney. He was apparently obsessed by the idea of walking between the twin towers from the moment construction on them began.
Why is the event interesting enough to deserve to be remembered? Like all theater, it was fleeting and transitory, yet it created an image of beauty that those who witnessed it never forgot.
From the grim aftermath, we know that the towers themselves were transitory. Like twin Towers of Babel, they aspired to touch the sky and yet they were so easily destroyed by those evil men.
And I guess it teaches us that everything we create and build and achieve, no matter how grandiose and significant it may seem, is transitory in this world of ours.
According to the movie, the event changed Petit in some fundamental way. For a short time, he became a star. He broke up with his girlfriend and his relationships with his loyal helpers also ruptured. I wish the movie had delved more into the aftermath. One extra included on the Dvd is an animated version of the story intended for children. It's almost more moving and resonant that the movie itself.
In the end we're left with the unforgettable image of a man walking, so it appears, on thin air, suspended in space a quarter of a mile in the sky.

Maggie Kean finds the body of her elderly neighbor, Elizabeth Boyer, blocking her septic tank at the beginning of this poorly-plotted book. Hunky detective Sam Villari shows up to investigate. He seems pretty incompetent and Maggie decides to look for the killer herself, which she proceeds to do in a completely haphazard and silly way. The two grandchildren of the deceased butt in as possible suspects. Maggie and Villari exchange some kisses, even though she thinks he suspects her as the killer -- and despite the fact that he smokes. The smooches with Mr Ashtray Mouth are pleasant for both parties and he invites her to meet his stereotypical Italian-American family. Mamma makes spaghetti and likes Maggie. Maggie likes spaghetti. Some more investigating happens and vague clues emerge. Threats are issued. More smooches. A climax of sorts happens. Someone or other is exposed as the killer and some kind of motive is offered. And then this entirely predictable and utterly absurd book ends and the scene is set for the next in the series. Hopefully the author will prosper and write another 60 books about the irrepressible Maggie. Her fans will rush to buy them for 99 cents apiece. Everyone will be happy. But for me, the series ends here with book one. Enjoy!

Listening to this recording is such a bitter-sweet experience. Amy Winehouse had the voice and the musical talent to build a career for the ages. Unlike so many pop divas, her genius was built to last. She could have become an Ella Fitzgerald-like figure -- a towering icon. If only. If only the self-destructive part of her psyche could have been brought under control. You read the liner notes of this CD and you see the photos of the intrinsically lovely but deeply damaged person -- you see the signs of personal destructiveness on her body. And you sigh for what might have been.

I don't think this was Amy's best work. I didn't love all the arrangements. But it shouldn't have mattered. She should have had many years to do better and better, to nurture and grow that talent, to fulfill that huge potential.

What I do like about the choice of music is the way she was consciously placing herself as a link in the chain of a grand musical tradition. There are songs here from the 1930s, from the 1950s and 1960s -- and brand new compositions. There are really lovely moments. Even the failures are interesting. You can tell she thought about this music and engaged fully with it.

What a terrible pity.

While I definitely enjoyed this quick, steamy novella, and I definitely appreciate anytime one of my favorite authors gives me just a little bit more of a series I absolutely adore, this installment didn't quite measure up to the full length novels that came before it. I really loved Craig, a character who was obviously unappreciated and overlooked up to this point. The sexy noncommittal bartender drew me in right out of the gate. Rain, too, was quite captivating. The eccentric, overly-emotional romantic is unlike any of Samantha Young's other leading ladies. The chemistry was evident, the story was unpredictable, sexy and fun.  I just think this novella's length prevented the author from being able to really dig deep and execute an emotionally layered plot as she typically does. I felt their attraction, I enjoyed their original, refreshingly different storyline but it just doesn't compare to the epic,  unforgettable, earth-shattering romances between Joss and Braden, Jo and Cam, Ellie and Adam, etc. The drama felt a little contrived, but One King's Way is still a cute extra. I Wish You Were Mine started off slow for me. First, I loathe love triangles. Aside from cheating, they are one of my automatic no-go's in books. But, its Lauren Layne, and I trust her. I will say for the first 35-45% of the book, I was losing faith fast. It was slow. I felt like knocking the characters heads together. I actual got to the point when I was like "Yo, Mollie is a great girl and if you are too dumb to give it a shot, she deserves better anyway". I actually wanted to write a character that would come in and totally sweep Mollie off her feet and away from this angsty crap. And while you realize that Madison, the ex wife/sister, is no saint, I still struggled with the fact that Jackson was married to Mollie's sister. I don't know if I would be okay with that if I were Mollie (just thinking about having sex with someone my sister had sex with creeps me out...). This book was heavy on the angst too, which I didn't expect since its not an NA book. But, what made it work for me? The office bromance! I loved getting peeks at other Oxford men!

Overall, I wanted better for Mollie than Jackson. Maybe if Jackson put more into fighting for Mollie? I'm not sure but I wanted him to do more. Perhaps I have my expectations of fictional men set too high? Its totally possible, but I think Mollie deserves better.

Irene decides to open Irenes Closet, a haute couture consignment store, but Adelle is upset that her daughter will be selling clothes someone else has worn.  Two hours before her shop was to begin its grand opening, Irene discovers the dead body of Loraine Sellers, one of her mothers friends, in a closet in her shop with a bullet in her head.  A short time later, another friend of her mother, Susana Delgado, is found murdered in Irenes shop.  Andrew Iglesias, the Chief of Police, is in charge of the official investigation and advises Irene to stay out of it.  Irene is compelled to continue her own investigation because she suspects her mother might be in danger and before long, she finds herself in over her head and in danger.

This vacuum is a big beast. I mean, seriously, it's the giant of canister vacuums. It's also on the heavy side. This is not a compact canister vacuum.

I've noticed vacuum cords getting shorter and shorter over the years. Cost savings for the manufacturer? I don't know the reasoning, but I do know it's irritating to need to plug your vacuum into two different outlets just to do one room. You won't have that problem with this vacuum. The cord is insanely long, as is the vacuum hose. This one will easily stretch out and do multiple rooms without a change of outlets.

Suction is fantastic. This will suck up my throw rugs if I'm not careful.

For me, it's a little too much vacuum. My entire house is laminate and tile, no carpets, and so I don't need such a big beast of a vacuum. I find it a little unwieldy for daily use.

The other thing I'm not crazy about is going back to needing replacement bags. When I opted to try this vacuum, I didn't notice that it's not bagless. I've had bagless vacuums for well over a decade now, and I'd forgotten what a nuisance (and an expense) it is to keep replacement bags on hand all the time.

If you have carpets and a lot of traffic with pets and such, this will probably be an ideal vacuum for your needs.

After reading and really enjoying book one of the Whiskey Nights series I was thrilled Hawk would be getting his own story. Unfortunately, for me, the plot and heroine fell a little flat.

Hawk caught my attention in Wasted during scenes at the bar. From his interactions I knew immediately he was a man that would make a good hero, a good savior. Being a firefighter, Hawk feels the need to save and protect. This came through beautifully in his character. And while I thought a love connection was going to made with the comical Haley, I understand the author's choice of choosing someone like Amber to catch Hawk's eye. Understanding doesn't mean I agree necessarily, because I was hoping for someone to be Hawk's equal.

Amber was in need of saving. Her story saddens the reader enough to feel for her but there were times it felt like too much wallowing and not enough reasons why. I never felt a connection with her character, I never felt as though she became Hawk's equal. She was always just someone in need of saving and she filled the role of damsel.

Ignited turned out to be a completely different book than what I was expecting. Where Wasted was laced with humor and witty dialogue I felt this book lacked in that very much. The dialogue didn't feel as clean to me but instead clunky in places. I found myself skimming through parts rather being immersed in the words. I still find Mason and Lexi to be great characters, I'll keep a soft spot for Hawk in my heart, and still look forward to reading the story of confident, sassy Seren in the next book of the series.

Couldn't finish reading it. Poorly written. Stone doesn't know the difference between "lay" and "lied." "Lied" means some told an untruth in the past. The conjugation is lie-lay or lay-laid. People "lie" down but "lay" down in the past. Holy cow. And please, please, please "all right" is ALWAYS two words! The constant moving back and forth between first person narratives within the same chapter is dizzying. Either write in the third person, or at least flesh out a chapter for each person's narrative. The book is amateurish. Either get an editor (even a friend who knows what they're doing), or get a style book and study it.

This is my honest review.*  Rough Around the Edges is actually a very seamlessly crafted and well paced love story.  Cuban-American Alejandro Jamison, retired Army Ranger, has returned to the Miami barrio where he grew up.  He spends his retirement pay and his time running a recreation center for the neighborhood youth.  It's the great passion of his life, until he meets Dr. Kristen Helton, who works at the neighborhood clinic.  She's everything he isn't - rich, socially prominent, once a high-achieving student and now a passionately dedicated healer.  They both feel the sparks, and they both see the social obstacles from the beginning.  Neither Alex nor Kristen can pull away and make it stick, and thus begins the bumpy road to their HEA.  Thankfully, this is no fairy tale, it's a grown-ups' love story in which the main characters act more than agonize.  They face their challenges, own their choices, and are true to their values.  I enjoyed getting to know Alex and Kirsten and their chosen place in the Spanish-speaking Miami barrio. I'd like to read more by this author.

There is so much that people have wanted in a great coffeemaker. They can be either a hit for drinkers, or more of a burden, because it doesn't fulfill the needs to deliver in regards to taste and quality. When it has shown for Keurig is that they have made some excellent ones with their K-Cup coffeemakers. Some have been delivering well overall from the classic K-Cup Coffeemaker, the Special Edition which worked so well, and many of them with the newer 2.0 models. But overall they have had ones that haven't made the mark that well, and this is one of them. The Keurig Mini Plus maintains itself as a simple and convenient way to have your K-Cups for one person. Yet it has been more of a problem to take care of than the other basic Keurig models. One problem is that you really get very bad taste after you clean it, by taking care of numerous brewing cycles, and you wouldn't know when it would be alright to have a cup. Another problem is that it doesn't brew as strong of a cup after one use. You honestly firmly do get better from other Keurig models, and I would recommend passing this one up.

Price: D+

Convenience & Setup: C

Overall: C-

There is no question that when it simply has came down to great coffee for the K-Cup machines, Green Mountain has made some excelente coffees for all to try, some are good, and some honestly could be just better not just in price, but also in flavor. Their Southern Pecan coffee isn~t actually a strong cup in taste. Pratically, it is mild and not as ntty as some of the other blends of coffee. It does taste well, but actually could have a bit ore into it to blend in the taste of the mild roast, like a sweet pecan glaze that handles into a strong cup for the day. It does handle mostly well, but Green Mountain has honestly made better blends that make it up like their Breakfast Blend and their Nantucket style as well. If you do want good coffee it Works well, but more honestly could have been added.

Price: B-

Taste & Quality: C

Overall: C+

BIND ME BEFORE YOU GO is a quick little BDSM-ish read.  I say BDSM-ish because while there are a couple of scenes in a BDSM club, theres not a whole lot of BDSM going on, apart from the Shibari rope bondage.  Im not familiar with Shibari, but it sounded like the author did her homework and she explained it fairly well.  When David was explaining the purpose behind it, about how it binds you to your partner which in turn binds them to you, I found it interesting and sweet.

Because of how quickly the story moves and the gaps in time, I didn't really feel a connection between David and Cassidy.  Both of them have their issues, but where Cassidy is open to the possibility of love, David has closed himself off.  He insisted she trust him and open up about her past, but he never offered her the same courtesy.  Because of all his past relationships, when Cassidy declared her love for him, he rejected it and hurt her in the process.

BIND ME BEFORE YOU GO is told in dual POVs and while its part of the Serve series, it can be read as a stand-alone.  It comes with a nice HEA for David and Cassidy, and Id classify it as an insta-love given the storys short time frame.

FIRST NIGHT is a very quick read about two strangers brought together by a mutual friend, who spend just one night together.  Julia runs a bar and is dealing with the financial aftermath of her ex-boyfriend's departure.  At least that's what I assume has happened because it was a little vague.  When Clay walks into her San Francisco bar, she hopes he's exactly the distraction she needs.  Even better, he lives in New York and a one-night-stand is all she's looking for.  But their one night was so hot and so full of passion that it left them realising it simply wasn't enough and the story ends with Clay inviting Julia to spend a weekend in New York with him.

FIRST NIGHT is a prequel novella in the Seductive Nights series.  It's a very quick read filled with fun flirting and hot sex but not much else.  I enjoyed it and I'm looking forward to learning more about Julia and Clay's past, present and future.

2 "Coming Home" Stars

The premise to Down to You was really interesting, but the way the story played out just didn't live up to my expectations. It was much shorter and a lot less angsty than I anticipated. While I enjoyed parts of the story, overall I just didn't feel connected to the characters or their story.

Brant and Holly have been divorced for a couple of years after having been married for about a decade. Now it's Christmas time and Brant wants to spend it with his whole family but can't seem to get through to his ex-wife that he wants her back. Holly is trying to move on but is finding it impossible because she's still in love with her ex-husband. With the help of their friends, they are pushed toward each other and have to finally come to terms with what happened in their marriage.

Holly and Brant's story is told in the present in both of their pov's while flashbacks are used to show how they met and fell in love and eventually divorced. I liked how this was done. It helped tell their story while letting me experience it with them. What didn't really work for me was that the whole  reason for the destruction of their relationship was flimsy and honestly a bit baffling. It's like they never spoke to one another after the problem started and I just don't see how that's possible. It also seem unrealistic that this situation would have lasted two years. I would have enjoyed this story a lot more if it was fleshed out a bit more and their relationship would have had a more understandable breakdown and not such an easy reconciliation after so much time had passed.

ARC provided for honest review.

2 "Off Limits" Stars

Across the Hall is a story that used two of my favorite tropes: brother's best friend and fresh out of prison. While there were definitely parts that I enjoyed, overall, I had a difficult time connecting with either character or their relationship.

Jude is not your average parolee. Growing up wealthy and in charge of a fashion network at as a young adult, he's out of prison early after being convicted of involuntary manslaughter. Now back home and running his empire out of his apartment for a month while he's on house arrest, he realizes that he now lives across the hall from one of his best friends from college and his sister. Having been warned off of Jillian, he doesn't expect to try and defy his friend-until he sees her.

Jillian is back from studying abroad in Paris. Trying to pick up the pieces of her heart that she left back in Paris as well as finding a job she loves are her only goals. But when she meets Jude, sparks fly. Knowing that her brother will eventually forgive her, she and Jude begin a relationship. But when her past comes back and secrets are revealed, she's left wondering if Jude is really worth it.

Jude and Jillian have some major heat together and I enjoyed their sexy times. Over all though I just didn't feel much of anything in regards to the storyline in general. The twist could have been really interesting but all the drama was resolved really quickly and much of it seemed to lack emotion or intensity. I think I had a hard time with the believability of the over arching plot line which made the rest not feel very realistic either.

There are quite a few bad reviews of these towels at the front of the review batch.  These reviews say that they are not absorbent, that they just move water around, that they are pretty but don't wash well, etc.  Well, I am here to say that they work reasonably well as kitchen towels.  My husband and I agreed to wash these first, before we decided to use them.  I find that when I wash kitchen towels (or other towels in general) before I use them, they become more absorbent.  Towels become more absorbent after they are washed because they are freed of the chemicals put on them to make them nice looking and perfectly straight in the package.  So after I washed these, I used these to clean up water in my kitchen.  The ones with the dark brown waffle print did not work well at all, but the ones with the plaid, stripe and circular white patterns seemed to absorb water as well as a paper towel does.

But now, for the real reason that I bought these towels, when I saw them displayed.  They were brown, and so pretty, and it's near Halloween so I ACTUALLY THOUGHT-hey, these towels would make great DO-RAGS!

And yes, the longer ones that are the normal kitchen towel size work well for that.  I have the one with the circular white print on my head now, it will match perfectly with my redneck trailer trash Halloween outfit I plan to wear.  They go very well with the bright red hair I currently sport. So if you like Do-Rags, or want to tie your long, abundant hair back, these kitchen towels do double duty in fashion as well.

As for the real little towel-I just could not find a use for it.  I don't think it's even good to try to recycle it as a washcloth, it is in the brown waffle print which really did not hold water.

From the moment they saw each other there was chemistry. Ashlynn couldn't move when her eyes locked with Chase. She had to know him. This is suppose to be a summer fling. Chase doesn't do relationships, hell the man doesn't date! Ashlynn, had a bad break up a few months back and isn't looking for love. She wants to have fun and experience a summer fling. They are both headed in the right direction with that. All they have is a month to spend together before they go back to the real world, which for them is hundreds of miles away. Her back in school in Georgia. Him, starting his NASCAR career in North Carolina.

They make the best of their time together. They take things slow, get to know each other and become each others world in this short time. Eventually the end of the month approaches and its time to part ways.  Heartbreaking? Yes. Hard to do? for sure.

Will they keep in touch?
Will they see each other again?

With life and priorities how will they maintain a connection?

I was sucked into the world of Chase and Ashlynn. Adorable story and I am eager to see what happens next.

I knew that Erin Noelle would do Scarlet and Mason's children right, and boy howdy, did she!!  Everett is everything that is his mother and father with a bit of just himself to accentuate.  He and his sister grew up in the rock music world and inherited the talent and ability to make beautiful music as well.  And Everett inherited the intense physical attractiveness to get the attention of beautiful Belle.  Their mutual attraction was instantaneous and smoking hot!  Although there was the impediment or two with their relationship, Everett possessed a depth and maturity that belied his natural age, and his ability to express his intense and sure feelings for Belle was quite amazing and heart-tingling.  Perhaps because of their main impediment, something happens that shouldn't have created an angry gulf between them as it did, but as is often the case, it just made the getting back together and working things out all the better and steamier.  Without dropping teasers, I have to say that the high point of the book for me was when my man Mason came out of nowhere, stepped up to the plate, and gave this couple the edge they needed to see through the fog & misconceptions to the true and abiding love they held for each other.  I would have thought it would be Scarlet who played such an essential role, but it thrilled me to see Mason be the man and father that I knew was in him.  Such a lovely story that, perhaps, a reader could begin to think was not going to do it for them, but comes through in the end.  Everett and Belle's attraction, joy, thrill, and adoration of each other spark your heart, make you smile and feel good all over for days after reading the very last word.  Thank you, Erin Noelle, for putting such a beautiful exclamation point on this family - - although there is still twin Ashlynn . . .

Being back in Adam's world made me nostalgic for the feeling I got the very first time I read the Shattered Hearts series.  We've gotten glimpses of Chris and Claire but for those of us who are and always will be #TeamAdam, this was a great surprise from Cassia Leo.

Now 32, Adam is at the top of his surfing game but struggling to balance his dream job with those of a family.  He and Lindsey have have had their ups and downs but have always emerged stronger.  With a new baby on the way, she is pushing him to retire.

Most of this book is really Adam's struggle to define himself.  If he retires, can he be happy giving up his dream?  I'll admit, I shook my head a few times at his decisions but then found myself sympathetic to him again.  At first, Lindsey came across a bit whiny but then I realized how much she has given up for Adam and I had no clue how they were going to resolve their issues and remain happy together.

Adam is a great father and it was lovely to watch him with his girls, corny jokes and all.  There are some sexy scenes, some funny ones, and some that make my heart squeeze (both good and bad).

For the fans of the series, reading this book really brought home how different Adam is from Chris.  Definitely not a bad thing but it did bring a lot of peace to know he and Claire both wound up with the people they were supposed to.

Any Adam lover will adore this book.  And even if you were #TeamChris, I think you'll enjoy being back in the Shattered Hearts world

I have to say, it's the plot and not the writing that kept me reading this book to the end. I stopped about halfway through and read the reviews. This is something I've never done before, but I was having qualms and wanted to see what my peers thought.
 So, I'll weigh in with one thing that others have said as well. Way too many metaphors, many of them corny at that.
 I didn't mind the explicit violence, and as a rule I don't mind well-placed sex references. I'm a big fan of wit inserted in fiction and only if it's done right. First of all, it has to be truly witty, and second of all it has to be judiciously sprinkled throughout. Just like to much salt on food, too much silliness in the thriller makes the whole thing hard to swallow.
 The entire character of Natalie from beginning to end was a distraction from the beautifully crafted storyline. I enjoy books where the civilian is involved in an investigation, but the probability that two serious detectives working on a lethal case, would have Natalie as their third detective through the entire book detracts from the entire thing... Also, her incessant potty mouth adds nothing to the book. In fact, we don't really get to know her. It is possible for a writer to take someone who begins the tale as a dingbat and through the story redeem and rehabilitate her so that we begin to understand and appreciate what she brings to the story. But even the part she plays at the end is not enough... I still saw just a very dumb, very crude, one dimensional character.
My final thought is that some of the dilemma in this book might be caused by the author trying, unsuccessfully, to blend a cozy mystery with a hard-boiled police procedural thriller. I think he will produce a better book if he chooses the police procedural thriller and leaves the silliness out. But this is one opinion. I have read mysteries and thrillers of various types exclusively for over 45 years. There were plenty of people who absolutely loved this. I am no prude, but the rhetoric has to be smarter. This was slapstick.
I may read another of Kelly's books because I do believe he will grow as an author. Telling a good story is art, and not everybody has it in them.

My only issue is that it takes 4 AA Alkaline batteries to get to 6 volts and these are not rechargeable.  The rechargeable batteries are only rated of 1.2 volts time four batteries would get you to only 4.8 volts.  While rechargeable batteries will fit, you will get a reduced voltage which I THINK would result in lower speeds?

I returned this to Amazon and bought the 4.6V version (grey body instead of black).  It came with a sealed battery pack and charger base for the pack. Now these batteries have a poor reputation for long life but I found what I consider to be a great work around.  I called Dremel and for only $5 pluse $2.50 shipping you can get a battery pack that accepts your 4 AA rechargeable batteries and fits perfectly into the 4.6 volt model.  Now I can simply remove the drained batteries from the battery pack, replace them with spare recharged batteries and I am ready to go.  And doing this is cheaper than buying a spare sealed 4.6 v pack.

Emily fell in love with him when she was 6 years old and when she turned 18 she went to Jakes bedroom changing her and his life forever.
He was beaten and thrown out of the house by Emilys brother AJ without knowing the consequences of that night. Everyone was filled with regrets and now that he is back , all their lives will once again change.
The plot is engaging and the characters are complex. The story is filled with suspense, bad guys, hunky good guys and of courses romance.
But its also a story about family,  loyalties, integrity  and sacrifices. Not everything is black and white and not everyone finds their happiness. Much like life which is what makes this one a very touching audiobook.
The narrator, Carson Beck, once again does a great job and brings the story to life.

These cards are reasonable.  They are not going to look like professionally printed cards.  Punching them out is somewhat of a pain.  You have to fold each edge twice to get a clean removal. You have to be careful or the paper will tear. They are good for things that will change, or when you need just a few cards with each piece of information.

The Avery software online requires you to give them your email address.
The software is pretty robust, you can do a lot of designing.  It will also let you save your final project as a PDF onto your computer so you can print more later without having to call up the software again.
There were a lot of premade cards on the software and you can import your own photos or images.
There was no way to select for just black and white designs, this would be a nice option.

The actual cards say template 8869, the directions say 8373.  Both worked.

I sent these through a laser printer (against the directions, which clearly say for Inkjet only).  No problems when printing the first side.  When trying to print on the backside about half the time one of the cards would come loose and jam the printer.  I do not suggest ignoring the directions and using these in a laser printer.

In the inkjet printer they were fine.

If you plan on printing in color, get the white ones.  On the Ivory the colors were a bit off.

This card is a good value, it is fast for the price and size (I have a brand name version with about the same write speed that cost twice as much).  There was no write speed listed here, or on the manufactures website, which I find supremely annoying.

 I will tell you it does NOT write fast enough to record  Full HD video on a Canon T5i (1,920 x 1,080 (1080p) at 30  frames per second) in spite of the claim here on the website.  Write speed is really, really important for using in a camera. It is less important when accessing information from the card (so for example using it on a phone for apps).  It is fast enough to take photos or video on my Android phone, but it does not keep up with the Canon.

I will say that your speed may vary depending on the device you are using, some of the devices themselves cannot take advantage of the speed.  It is overkill to be using this with a device that cannot read at these speeds.

Nevertheless, for simple storage this is a good value.  Not good enough for really intense photography.

Its certainly different than all the others, but for that part of me that likes having detail and information, I just wish the book was a bit longer and we got a longer glimpse into the life that Ryan and Natalie have in front of them. Hopefully well get to see how things play out in subsequent volumes, I know Im definitely interested!

Last Chance was a definite four star read. Ms. Wood took characters that I grew fond of in the first book and made me fall in love with them. Im still not the biggest fan of Natalie, however I love Ryan and Liam, and the fact that they're not your stereotypical rocker bad boys, its a nice change of pace!

I loved this story!  Matthew Weston and Brandon(his story will be told in the second book of the series) own the Onyx club.  Theyve been friends for a long time and in the past, have shared more than just a friendship, theyve also shared women.

Matthew likes to be called Matthew, not Matty, or Matt, just Matthew. Hes 38, arrogant, dominant and the ladies love him. He does have one rule, not to sleep with his staff. To him, woman are just a means to an end, there for him to use for sex whenever he wants. One day, his whole life changes when a woman called Ella applies for a job at the club.

Ella is 22 and just ordinary looking, plain. When Matthew first sees her, she looks like a homeless junkie and even though he usually doesnt care, he cant shake off the feelings he gets when hes around her. She is running from a very dark past and needs the job more than most people do.

As Ella settles into her job, the relationship between employer and employee changes and we see a softer side of Matthew come out. Ella is the only person he doesnt mind calling him Matt which is one of the many things he doesnt understand about his feelings towards her.

As the story develops, we see a change in Matthew as he has someone he wants to care about and also, a change in Ella as she learns to trust someone completely with her life. If anyone has a reason never to trust anyone ever again, its Ella.

I loved the end of the story too and as a debut novel, its excellent. Im looking forward to reading more from this author.

This story was okay. The characters and story were interesting. This was a quick read, the story is pretty short. Ginger has headed up to Alaska to make it out to her dad's hunting cabin to try and find something he left her. She has almost no money to be able to do it and there are taxes on the land as well. Her father has passed away from cancer and so the medical bills and debt are high. She is referred to Brock for help making it out to her father's cabin. Brock has just become Clan leader and has been told that he needs a mate. As soon as he sees Ginger he knows that she is his mate but he is not sure if he is ready for one and so has no plans to move on that yet.
The transitions in the story could be a little better. It is nothing that really hurts the story or makes things confusing. The transitions are not very smooth, sometimes it feels a little abrupt for me. Things happen quickly between Brock and Ginger because of the situation they are in and the length of the book. It's not as smooth and believable as some that I've read but it's definitely not the worst and it's not that bad. You just have to let it go that it happens quickly. The characters are pretty well written and don't have holes in them. The sex is fairly explicit but not super often. Overall it was a pretty good story.

This was an enjoyable, quick read. Angus and Poppy move a little faster than the other Rescue bears. They get matched on the app and decide to meet right away rather than chatting through the app and getting to know each other first. Poppy is at a place with her job, where she knows something is wrong but hasn't figured out what it is yet, and so decides to go meet Angus and figure out what to do about her job. Angus and Poppy both feel the connection between them but Angus decides to not move too quickly because he doesn't want Poppy to regret anything. I enjoyed the way that this story flowed and built the relationship. There is some action in this story to keep your attention as well. The sexual chemistry is very strong through the whole story. The sex is explicit but not very frequent. It is the third story in this series but can be read as a standalone story. The other characters in the previous stories are in this one as well. We get to see quite a bit of them and so if you have read the previous stories than you get added enjoyment of getting to catch up some with the rest of the crew but it isn't something that you have to have read to fully enjoy and engage in this story.

Before I start this review, I have to be perfectly honest and say I am not a fan of Ben's character. He seemed like a good guy at the beginning of Connected, but as more was revealed about the man he really was in Torn, I liked him less and less. It is going to be very difficult for his character to be redeemed in my eyes. I hoped this novella would do it, and while it did, in the end, start him down the path of redemption, I was definitely a little underwhelmed overall.

I didn't feel like there was a whole lot of new story in Blurred. We got some journal entries and more information from Ben's time after his "death," but that really felt like about all. It wasn't anything I couldn't have really inferred on my own from the events of Torn. It definitely wasn't a happy book. The majority of the focus is on Ben dealing with all the things that are wrong in his life since his return. It did make me a little sympathetic for him at times. The man has been through a lot and I have to feel a little bad for him, even if I think he handled everything very poorly. Even after getting a peek inside his head, I can't excuse his actions.

As I write my review, it sounds like I disliked this book. I didn't. Don't get me wrong. It was good, just not great, for me. Had it been about a character I liked, it might have been a different story. But, all in all, it's an interesting introduction to Ben and Bell's in Frayed. Hopefully this means we'll jump right into the story at the beginning of that book. I don't need another look at Ben's past. It's unflattering and doesn't help me like him any. If anything, it proves to do the exact opposite. Blurred was a very quick read and it did fill in some of the blanks in Ben's story. Fans of the series will undoubtedly want to read it. I'm really done with Ben's past, however. I'd much rather focus on his future and, hopefully, his redemption.
