Julie Particka's Fall With Me took two of my favorite tropes  the fake relationship and the very real falling for a friend  and combined them together in a book that was utterly unputdownable for me. Was it predictable? Of course. Is that a bad thing? Not even a little bit.

Jenna and Sutton have known each other for years and once upon a time, there was a flicker of something more than friendship between them. He's her best friend's brother and she's had a crush on him forever. What she doesn't know is that he feels the same about her. When Jenna's boyfriend dumps her for her best friend, and Sutton's sister Lacey, neither of them are pleased about this relationship. Jenna's ex is a real dirt bag, but Lacey insists there's more to him and their relationship. Sutton and Jenna decide to team up and fake date to break them up. This pairing leads up to a whole lotta drama as feelings become more apparent and other truths are revealed.

Fall With Me was a short read, but a really enjoyable one. It was sometimes sweet, sometimes sexy and a good new adult book through and through. I really enjoyed the characters, even in those moments where I wanted to smack sense into them.

Jess is sick and tired of being a good girl. Single, geek, virgin, she decides this summer is a perfect time to make a change. Have a fling with a hot man. Cash in her V-card. When her brother Reid invites her for a month-long, all-expenses paid trip to Australia, she jumps at the chance. Upon arriving in Australia, she meets sexy, bad boy chef Jack, who makes her feel like being bad. Really bad.

Jack is sick of having meaningless flings. He doesn't want to be that guy anymore. When gorgeous, American Jess shows up at the cattle station where he works, he feels a spark, immediately. But, he also believes he's not good enough for her. He hides his feelings and tries his best to reign in his attraction to her, regardless of how frequently she flirts and throws herself at him. She has a bright future and he is a loser. He refuses to drag her down. But, they're damn near combustible when together and that's a pull that's difficult to resist.

This novella was short and sweet  and had just enough sexy to make it interesting. Told from both Jess' and Jack's POV, the reader gets a really good sense of each character, their background and motivation, and their true feelings. I know this was supposed to be Jess' book, but while I liked her, Jack stole the show for me. He absolutely charmed me. There was something vulnerable about him that I connected with strongly. Before was a total tease. I mean that in a good way, though. It gave a great introduction to the characters. I enjoyed it so much I immediately went to Amazon, bought Brash and devoured it, too. I needed more Jack and Jess in my life.

Leah is still nursing a broken heart after the demise of their two-month fling. Jason, on the other hand, is angry over Leahs assumption that he hadnt abandoned his playboy ways while they were still together. Despite the obvious chemistry between these two, both are stubborn in their belief that the other is at fault. Lack of communication, only serves to further keep this couple apart.

Between Jasons stubbornness over revealing the truth to Leah and Leahs unwillingness to hear him out, I found the storyline frustrating. Sharon Cullen perfectly captures the spirit of the Victorian murder mystery in her historical romantic suspense: THE RELUCTANT DUCHESS. For the fifth day in a row, Lady Sara Emerson is at the Duke of Rossmoynes door asking for an audience. Gabriel Ferguson, Ross, as the Duke is known to his friends, shuns society but finally caves in and agrees to see the very persistent Sara. After her cousin Merediths burial, Ross has told Saras family that if they ever needed his help, he would be there for them; he was betrothed to Meredith, and he understood how distressed they were after her murder. Ross is distraught when Sara shows him the reason for her visit: she has been receiving threatening letters mentioning Merediths demise, and Ross agrees to help her, along with the Scotland Yard inspector who investigated the case. If Ross had thought Sara determined, he never expected the quiet, bookish spinster to be such a force of nature. The Duke is a rather haughty man, and even two years after the death of his fiance, he has remained dour. Unassuming Sara is the polar opposite of Meredith, and yet he finds himself drawn to her, even more so as Saras safety becomes paramount, and he insists that living in his home would offer her more protection.

THE RELUCTANT DUCHESS is as much a romance as it is a Victorian murder mystery, and Ms. Cullen succeeds on both counts. The pace is somewhat leisurely as Ross and Sara investigate the murder, and doing so, they get to know each other better. In spite of their first impressions, they discover that they have a lot in common, but for the persistent shadow of Meredith. THE RELUCTANT DUCHESS has a rather Gothic feel, which surprised and delighted me, and I applaud the authors thorough research as she paints a most convincing portrait of Victorian society in all its aspects. The characters feel authentic, the romance evolves organically albeit not so smoothly, and I was kept guessing until the end as to whom the murderer was. Very well done!

SONG OF THE SOUTH is a delightful movie with good stories, good acting, and great songs. I originally saw it as a child. My mother took us to the theater to see it. The place was packed with noisy kids, but they all went quiet when Uncle Remus started telling his stories. In the intervening years, the dreaded Political Correctness has relegated this movie to the Disney Vault, although I was able to find an imported copy. I recently watched it for the first time in 35 years and you know what? There's nothing wrong with it. It might have some stereotypes but nothing offensive or even questionable. Think of Gone with the Wind or some of the old Shirley Temple movies or even Our Gang. I certainly wouldn't think twice about letting my own children watch it.

With that out of the way, SONG OF THE SOUTH is every bit as memorable as Pinocchio, another movie I just watched after too many years. In both cases, elements of the movies have entwined themselves around our collective consciousness. The Tar Baby, for example, is a metaphor I've heard used often. I use it myself. (Disney changed it to a Honey Baby on their Splash Mountain ride.) And who can forget Br'er Rabbit begging Br'er Fox and Br'er Bear not to toss him into the briar patch, which is just where he wanted to go. But the most memorable part of the movie has got to be Uncle Remus singing Zippity Do Da.

As I said, SONG OF THE SOUTH is just a delightful movie that's gotten a bum rap. If you get the chance to see it, by all means do!

I vividly remember watching HANS CHRISTIAN ANDERSEN on television many times as a young child.  It made a great impression on me then, and it still impresses me today.  Over the Thanksgiving holiday, multiple generations (including a passel of kids from 4 to 14) watched this classic, 1950s, movie musical together.  Everyone was enchanted.  Older generations shared their happy memories of this story with the younger ones.  And I was shocked and delighted to discover that I remembered the words to every song.

As stated in the opening frames of this film, HANS CHRISTIAN ANDERSEN is "not the story of his life, but a fairy tale about a spinner of fairy tales."  And what a charming fairy tale it is!  With outstanding songs by Frank Loesser, a brilliant performance by Danny Kaye, and gorgeous scenery that seems to leap right out of the pages of a fairy tale picture book, HANS CHRISTAN ANDERSEN captures the hearts and souls of old and young alike.  The wonderfully familiar and memorable songs get the entire family singing along.  I clearly remember the words to "I'm Hans Christian Andersen," "The Ugly Duckling," "Wonderful, Wonderful Copenhagen," "Thumbelina," "Inchworm," "The Emperor's New Clothes," and "No Two People (Have Ever Been So In Love)" from my childhood.  In fact, I have been singing some of these songs to my kids for as long as I can remember!

HANS CHRISTIAN ANDERSEN is a happy multi-generational family film that will give everyone warm fuzzies.  This is the perfect time of year for watching HANS CHRISTIAN ANDERSEN, but I would be thrilled to watch it anytime.  This beautiful, nostalgic musical brings up many happy memories and helps make new ones.  HANS CHRISTIAN ANDERSEN is MOST HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

I really wanted to like KICK-ASS.  The premise and the apparent message of ordinary people standing up to villains and crime and making a difference was very, very appealing.  But honestly, the only reason to watch KICK-ASS is the 3 fight scenes with the little girl. That's it. End of story. Of course, they are very violent and bloody, so if you can't imagine watching an 11-year-old girl stab, shoot, and slice the legs off of countless thug-types who deserve it, then there's no reason for you to watch KICK-ASS.

But let's say you've been tricked into seeing KICK-ASS or someone has threatened to post unflattering photos of you and your hamster on Facebook if you don't watch the entire flick.  So you're sitting there in an empty theater and what do you see? Well, for the first 30 minutes, you DO NOT see any superhero stuff. No, you see pointless drivel about how hard it is to be a nerdy teenager. You get to see the main character's masturbatory fantasies (literally and graphically). And you wonder how this schmuck could afford a $99 wet suit. Finally, right around the 30 minute mark, he dons his wet suit, gets beaten to a bloody pulp, and sent to the hospital where everyone believes he's gay. So now, not only is he a nerdy teen, he's a faux gay nerdy teen.

But I haven't mentioned the plot. Oh wait. For 33% of KICK-ASS, that IS the plot.  For the other 66%, it is a lot of gratuitous violence and gore.

I was really disappointed in KICK-ASS.  It could have been a really good, positive movie.  But it degenerated into teen angst, gratuitous violence, and copious blood pretty quickly.  Yes, there are some funny moments, and yes, the ending is actually satisfying, but overall, KICK-ASS is just disturbing, and I won't recommend it to anyone.

I love X-Files, but truly season 7 is the weakest so far, have no idea if it gets any worse in later seasons. There are several reasons why I just couldn't enjoy it as much as previous seasons.

With the destruction of the Syndicate and all previous mytharcs dropped, the new arc started in the last episode of season 6 just didn't play out well in first 2 episodes of season 7. This story line has gotten so much out of control and became so "philosophical," I simply couldn't understand what was going on. Same goes for "The Closure" episode which was supposed to finally end the mystery of Samantha Mulder's disappearance. It certainly didn't give me much closure except for confirming Samantha was in fact dead. What was "En Ami" about anyway? I liked last episode of the season, some brilliance from past seasons came back, but I felt that story deserved more screen time. Considering that this episode was meant to be the last of the show, it sure was a cliffhanger.

The handling of the relationship between Scully and Mulder was really irritating. I don't mind the idea of a platonic relationship between these two, but why then inject the unnecessary teasers and allude to their being intimate without actually confirming it? There is only so much teasing I can take. Also, why was Scully so depressed most of this season? She was so sad majority of the time, I just wanted to quit.

Finally, there were not that many truly good episodes that we came to love. Too many episodes had emotional and philosophical instead of regular investigative content. It doesn't mean I hated this season, but it definitely was way below the par.

I saw the original Planet of the Apes as a child, so I was pretty geared up to see this one.  While I won't say that I didn't enjoy it, if you're a fan of the classic film, then you might want to stick with that and give this one a pass.  For one thing, Mark Wahlberg was okay as Captain Leo Davidson, but he could have done so much more with the part.  His previous role as Bobby Shatford in The Perfect Storm proved he can act, but in this movie he was so stiff and wooden that someone could have slapped him and it wouldn't have had any effect.  Helena Bonham Carter did all right as Ari, and Michael Clarke Duncan was terrific as Attar, but other than Charlton Heston's uncredited cameo as the father of General Thade and Kris Kristofferson as Daena's father, most of the acting in this movie just left me cold.
My major issue with this film lies not with Tim Burton's directing--Semos knows that Burton can make a fairly decent movie every now and then, and the story in this one was okay--but with the ending.  It just came off as too contrived and hokey, and it really didn't strike me as a good way to open things up for a sequel.
In the end, I'll just say what I did at the start--if you're a newbie to the Planet of the Apes films, then go ahead and watch this one, but if you're a fan of the classic Apes movies, then pass this one up.

I have a couple of kitchen scales and they all take up too much room. Most scales have the body of the scale and then something that somehow sticks up that bounces up and down as you add weight. This scale is more like a bathroom scale that has one solid plane across the top surface. Nice.

This scale is about the size of a small tablet (smaller than an iPad, more like a Kindle Fire). It slides easily into a drawer or between other items in a cupboard. I love the fact that it doesn't take much space.

On on/off controls are easy to use and it's pretty easy to reset the tare. The weight displays in pounds, ounces, and one decimal place (for example, 1 pound 4.3 ounces).

This scale also has a kitchen timer. The timer isn't especially useful for me, but it's nice. I already have a timer on my oven, microwave, and phone. It's still handy though.

This is a very nice scale that does a good job and doesn't take up too much room in my kitchen.

This was the first book I have read by this author and although this is the third book in a series, you can definitely read this book as a standalone. I loved Adam and Mia. He is a tough-talking, Alpha cop and she is a beautiful redhead who doesnt take BS from anyone. I loved Adam and Mias near-constant fighting almost as much as I loved their incredibly hot sex scenes. These two cant stay away from each other even though they drive each other crazy when they're together. The book is told in a series of alternating POVs which I loved. Adam and Mia married young, and suffered through an incredibly painful tragedy. A series of unfortunate misunderstandings leads to their breaking up, but they never stopped loving each other. At times during the story, I found Mias behavior to be absolutely infuriating but I really grew to love her about half-way through the book! And Adam is amazing! All he wants to do is provide a home for Mia. He is a really good guy but he always says the wrong thing.

There is an exciting storyline and a very satisfying epilogue to Adam and Mias story. Sometimes, you need a break from all the wealthy billionaire/innocent heroine love stories with a story about two very down-to-earth and relatable characters and this is the perfect antidote. I am going to read the first two books in this series and I am looking forward to more stories from this author!

I read Freeing Asia and am a big fan of E.M. Abels writing. She writes real new adult characters, who are not perfect by any means and who are all looking to find themselves a little bit. There are connected characters in Breaking Shaun, but you absolutely can read this book without having read Freeing Asia (although I totally recommend it because its awesome) Breaking Shaun tells the story of Natalie and Shaun, Asias brother. He is a hot and sexy, gorgeous surfer, a total manwhore who is unapologetic in his behavior but in his defense, completely honest and open with the girls that he sleeps with. Full disclosure. but it doesnt make for any less drama on the part of the girls he leaves behind. He is NOT interested in any kind of lasting relationship at all.

Shaun then meets his match in the smart and sext Natalie. She has moved to town to get a fresh start and starts work as a bartender. She, too, doesnt believe in true love and uses guys for sex. Perfect match for Shaun, right? Natalie has her reasons for this behavior which we find out later in the story.

Shaun and Natalies group of friends like to party so there is lots and lots of wild nights out drinking and smoking pot. Shaun and Natalie start off as good friends and move towards a deeper relationship when they have the most mind-blowing sex of their lives. And Ms. Abel can write some SOMKING hot sex scenes! What I loved about the sexy times is that they are actually infused with some pretty deep feelings, despite what Shaun and Natalie might say about wanting to remain unattached.

As Natalie asserts:

Women like me don't fall for men like you. We don't come when you call, we don't beg for your attention and we don't confuse sex with love. Women like me, break men like you

Natalie and Shaun really do build a solid, caring friendship, and they both try to make the other a better person. Natalie encourages Shaun to move forward with this surfboard designs and Shaun encourages her to return to school to pursue her passion, photography. I absolutely love the beach-y setting of Breaking Shaun and the glimpses into the world of surfing. This is another warm, very sexy, well-written story with lots of heart. There is lots of partying but there is also a great story and strong characters. I love this author and hope there will be more books in this series!

Here is a summary of the book (SPOILERS ahead): He is deeply in love with her, but after a disastrous marriage to a dissolute cad, introduced to her by the hero, she has cold feet. She succumbs after a couple of chapters. Then neither of them has cold feet. In fact, all parts of their anatomy are quite hot. Then he gets cold feet because of health issues. She warms him back up and they live happily ever after.

Most of the book involves the H and h writhing in bed, muttering "You are going to KILL me."

I'd like more in a book.

Something more is tantalizingly offered in an opening series of letters from the hero, wooing the heroine long distance from his diplomatic duties in Russia. The letters are charming and witty and romantic. The hero hears, at one point, that the heroine has been seen in the company of a rival, and he says, "I know he's handsome, darling, but the fellow will bore you to death once you've stopped looking at him and started listening to him."

Unfortunately, the letters end before Chapter 1 begins. I had sort of a reverse problem from the one the hero mentioned. I enjoyed listening to the H and h in their letters more than watching them roll around in bed.

This is billed as a Maiden Lane novella, but it really is only tangentially related to the series. Godric and Megs, two characters I've enjoyed, have walk-on parts, but since this isn't their story, they seem like a generic gloomy guy married to a generic upbeat woman.

The story is quite generic, too. Viscount D'Arque's carriage breaks down as he is escorting his grandmother to visit relatives for Christmas, and he winds up an unwilling guest at a house party. While waiting for his grandmother to recover from pleurisy, he pursues Sarah, who is the oldest of Godric's half-sisters.

Sarah despises D'Arque, a first class rake, because she had a life-alteringly bad experience with a rake when she was younger.

D'Arque pursues her with annoying pick-up lines and crude innuendo. He is every man women meet in bars who make them roll their eyes as they try to avoid them.

But, she quickly changes her mind because he is kind to his grandmother and dogs, plus he kisses well.

He decides he loves her because she doesn't fall immediately for his charms and is apparently the only woman he's met who thinks he is obnoxious and sleazy.

The novella isn't bad, but I felt I'd read it a number of times before. Nothing beats a reformed rake, but this reformation seemed a stretch, as did Sarah's capitulation.

This little coffee maker is just what I needed. I don't drink coffee while I'm in the car, but I needed help because I am the odd one at home and at work. Everyone else drinks regular coffee. I can't handle caffeine, so I drink only decaf. This little gem takes up very little space, so I can squeeze it into our limited counter space next to the big pot used by the rest of the family. It will also help when the whole family goes to a cabin in the mountains and to the beach. I can take this little device along and no longer will I have to dilute the "real" coffee enough for me to drink.

The coffee brews quickly and stays hot quite a while. The one-cup coffee maker I am currently using at work makes the cup hot, but the coffee is never better than tepid. I might have to get another one of these Mr. Coffee makers to use at work.

I am not a fan of filter-less coffee pots, but that won't be an issue unless I do take the pot to work where I will have to make a trip to the bathroom to clean out the filter.

The cup is easy to clean, but since I won't be traveling with the cup, I will experiment with our regular coffee mugs.
ADDITION:
After using the coffee maker for a while, I'm revising the review and taking away a star. There is much I still like about the little guy, but getting water into it is more trouble than it should be. The opening is so small and arranged poorly so that it is impossible to use a cup to pour water into it and there is a lot of spillage to clean up. One solution would be to haul the bulky thing over to the sink. Instead, I keep a cream pitcher handy and use it to pour water into the machine.

I've read a few novellas recently--some of them really excellent. This one doesn't rank among the top tier for several reasons. For instance the couple could have easily avoided some of their difficulties (get a room, for Pete's sake) and the hero could have reached the only sensible conclusion through the maturity he gained during the story rather than requiring an outside event's wake-up call.

But, the story had something great going for it. The couple actually conversed and got to know each other and enjoyed each other's company. Each admired the other. They clicked. They had an emotional connection which they recognized and nurtured.

What a nice change from the many stories in which a couple fall in lust and never seem to progress to anything more.

I was pleasantly surprised by just how much content is loaded on this two disk DVD package. Not only do you get the complete concert but you get three other bonus features that are all about or over an hour long.

First, the concert. I've seen it twice in Vegas. This one was pretty good although, to me, she seemed a little tired during some of the performances. "I'm Alive" in particular wasn't very good. She pretty much doesn't care how "Love Can Move Mountains" turns out anymore. She just goes out there and sings whatever. But there are two fantastic performances and those are the Italian song and "River Deep."

The bonus features start with a "Tribute to the Fans" which is touching and also a little creepy. Some of the stories are heart warming and others make the people look a bit sad. One woman says she's had two miracles in her life and one is beating cancer and the other is meeting Celine. I mean...she's had NOTHING else happen in her life more important than meeting a celebrity? And the people that got Celine tattooed on their bodies need some kind of therapy. I think even Celine was creeped out by that.

Another bonus feature is the complete concert but back stage and it is absoutely fascinating what goes on back there and just how much energy is put in to putting on each show every day. The dancers all work extremely hard and Celine is running around non stop and never gets a break. The time she's off stage is spent rushing to put on the next dress. And you almost get to see a naked Celine in this.

The last feature is an hour of interviews with everybody who put the show together and everything that happened. Celine talks about her ugly blonde hair period. They also show some of the performance of the night when she lost her dad.

Great DVD. A must buy for any Celine fan.

I am VERY critical of Disney these days. They have turned out so much junk over the past several years that it is criminal. Mainly these sequels of their classics. Such complete failures are The Little Mermaid 2, Cinderella 2, Aladdin 2, Aladdin 3, The Hunchback Of Notre Dame 2, Pocahontas 2 ect. So when I heard a sequel to Peter Pan was coming out I rolled my eyes and prepared for another poor excuse for a movie. To my surprise, Return to Neverland is not only good, but I actually liked it better than the original movie! I can't believe I actually said that! And to think I LOVED Peter Pan was I was younger. This movie has beautiful animation, a pretty decent story, and nice voice acting. My only complaint is the voice of Peter. His voice is WAY too young sounding to fit his character model. Peter has the body of a teenager 15-16 years old. He's slightly more muscular in this than the original. And yet he sounds like he's 8 years old. Another downer is that Peter hasn't matured any. I know he doesn't age any in Neverland but sometimes he just get annoying with his childish antics. He looks too old to be such a brat. The music in this movie is also not so good. You forget it as soon as you hear it. But that aside, I highly enjoyed myself while watching this movie.

This is the first novella in the Rogue Vows series, another collaboration between Kendra Elliot and Melinda Leigh, two authors whose other works I love, and as expected, this one didn't disappoint either.
We're back in Solitude, a small town in Oregon and home to the Taylor family. Police officer Stevie Taylor is preparing for her wedding day when the murder of a popular TV celebrity brings chaos and danger to the quaint, little town. Can Stevie and police chief Zane Duncan, who is Stevie's fianc, find the culprit in time to enjoy their big day?
Although not really necessary as this works as a standalone short story, if you enjoy gripping but heartwarming romantic suspense stories, start with the Rogue River and Rogue Winter series and then enjoy this continuation.
Despite the fact that this is a novella, it has everything that you would expect from a full-length romantic suspense novel. Really enjoyable.

I currently have two tanks, a 55 gallon and a 30 gallon, and own quite a few Pet Magasin products. I have to say I have been happy with almost every one of them, too, because they have performed and keep performing despite being economical affordable. From bubblers to thermostats and more, the company has consistently come up with ways to make pet ownership easier and I appreciate that quite a bit.

With regard to the Ultimate PM-MID Glass Aquarium, I had been looking for an effective way to clean algae off the sides of my tank and this does so really well. Operation is very simple; the item has two sides to it. You put one on the inside of the glass and the other on the outside. The item attracts magnetically and holds very well, and the side for interior use has a rough, scrubber area. It does not take much effort at all to do your average cleaning, and continued scrubbing can remove stains that have been on for too long.

Another feature of this I like is that the interior side floats. That means that if you are cleaning and pull away, it does not detach and sink to the bottom. This makes the end of cleaning a lot easier and reattachment, if needed, a breeze. The cleaner does not grip too tightly, either, applying enough pressure to hold well but not enough to damage glass.

Bottom line is that I really like this. It is cost-effective and helps out with cleaning quite a bit.

Please note that this was provided as a sample in exchange for honest feedback. I take reviewing seriously because I buy based on suggestions, so this in no way impedes the reviewing process.

I am a fan of Phillipa Gregory's "The Other Boleyn Girl" novel, therefore I was really excited when I heard they were making a movie.  My friends who saw the movie in the theatre warned me that it was disappointing if you were a fan of the book (or if you had even read the book!) and they were not wrong.

This is a horrible adaptation.  "Loosely based" is a generous description of what this movie did to Gregory's work.  None of the characters are well developed, so you end up asking yourself "why did she/he do that" at critical points of the movie because you don't have the background provided by the book to understand the character's motivation.  Also, the movie is primarily about Anne Boleyn (Natalie Portman) whereas the book is about the other Boleyn sister (duh) Mary (Scarlett Johansen).  The book's focus on Mary was what made it an interesting take on the whole Anne Boleyn/Henry VIII saga--if you want to see something purely about Anne Boleyn watch "Anne of a Thousand Days" or even the recent Showtime "Tudors"--both are better.

I will say that this movie is beautiful to watch.  They obviously spent lots of money on costumes and sets, so it is a visually pleasing film.  This doesn't make up for the problems I've outlined above.  I would not recommend this movie to anyone who has read Phillipa Gregory's book.  Maybe I would recommend it to a casual viewer who has no other exposure to Henry VIII based works, but to anyone else, go find one of the better interpretations out there!

Sunshine Cleaning is a movie about ordinary people, trying to make their lives work out in a difficult world.  Rose (Amy Adams) is a single mom of a precocious 8 year old.  She was the head cheerleader in high school, but now her life has taken a turn for the worse, and she's cleaning houses to make ends meet.  Her sister Nora (Emily Blunt) is a wild child who is always losing her jobs because she isn't reliable.  Rose gets a tip from her boyfriend that there is money to be made in cleaning up crime scenes, and the sisters set up their own business.  Alan Arkin also stars as the girls eccentric father.

This movie was touching and a little bit sad--in the way that real life movies often are--with just enough sunshine around the edges to keep it from being depressing.  I think the two women were superb, they did a great job of capturing the emotions wrapped up in these women's difficult lives.  It wasn't depressing, but it was a movie you can really get emotionally involved with.

I would recommend this film to someone looking for a good art-house type movie with interesting characters.  It's also a good film for fans of Amy Adams and Emily Blunt to see them both do something completely different--this movie definitely shows off the talent of both actresses.

Edited to add:  It's been 11 months now and I just woke up to find it broken.  No slow dying or anything that would have given me warning.  Just stopped working. My Fluval canister filter died and I had to get something--FAST.  I bought this because it was more budget friendly.  Compared to my Fluval, it's loud.  Compared to the Fluval it moves the water forcefully enough that the smaller fish and my Betta, with his ridiculous fins, topple around.  It's just OK in that regard.  I'll probably end up with the Fluval canister in a few months, honestly.

I was initially unhappy but realized that I have to compare this to other filters in this style.  This isn't a canister filter.  Compared to other "over the top" style filters I've had over the years, this is the best one I've ever had.  It is quieter than previous filters of this style.  It's easier to manage and clean.  It moves water well and quickly.  It's more solid and not as cheaply made.  It's easier to put together, clean, and reassemble.

If you are replacing something expensive, just buy an exact replacement because this will disappoint you.

If you've always had this type of filter, you should buy this one because it's very good and comparably quiet.

If you're looking for a cheap, but decent emergency filter to have on hand, this is perfect for that.  That's what this will become for me.

Although the central heating furnace for my old house is in the basement, there are no heat radiators down there so it gets very cool in the winter. For several years I have had a small cube-shaped "ceramic" heater from Wal-Mart to take the chill out if I spend any time there, but I have noticed not very much heat comes out of that. In fact last winter I accidentally left it on for 24 hours and could barely notice any heating effect at all in the basement as a whole. I was pretty disgusted.

This heater uses the same watts of power, yet the hot air just pours out of it... and there is no fan to wear out. Electric heat is almost always an expensive way to go, but at least this thing is doing something for the money.

The whole body of it is really a cluster of convection chimneys which take advantage of the fact that hot air rises to circulate air very effectively (and very silently) through the heater. If I just washed my hair, I could dry it in a couple of minutes over the blast of hot air coming out of this heater. They call this a radiant heater, but it actually gives off very little radiant heat. It is mostly a hot-air heater.

The overall construction is rather sturdy metal; it has a very nice solid feel to it. I deducted a couple stars because I feel the plastic legs/feet/wheels are not as solid looking as the rest of it. For my relatively rough use in the basement, I wish it had more rugged feet. In light of this product costing a lot more than some other similar heaters I've seen, I think it SHOULD have more rugged feet. The feet after all are somewhat important for safety... you don't want the hot unit falling over unexpectedly, even if it is not exactly red hot.

But when I review a product I must consider value for the dollar, and in my opinion this product costs way too much. No way am I going to pay $3 or more per 12 ounce box of this when I know I can buy a 16 ounce box of pasta locally for $1 or less. If I want fiber I'll eat raisin bran.

$5 apiece for 2.8 ounce chocolate bars? Come on! MAYBE if they were really something outstanding, but these taste like very ordinary quality chocolate to me. In fact, I much prefer the taste of Hershey's own "Symphony Milk Chocolate with Almonds and Toffee" bars over these... and they cost well under 1/4th the price per ounce.

My husband is not a "jeans" guy...his idea of casual is Khaki slacks with a dress shirt...or maybe he will slum it in a professorial-looking sweater on "casual day" at the office.  We could only get him to wear jeans for camping trips with the family...and even then it was a fight.  Getting him to try these on was a coup in and of itself!  I'm so glad he did!  He found them to be nothing like other jeans he has worn.  The stretchy denim left him marveling at the difference between his stiff, uncomfortable 'camping' jeans and these, which are truly ultra-soft (and get softer with washing)!  He also thinks they look much more presentable than other jeans he has tried/worn and he was relieved because they are going to be enforcing a "jeans day" on Fridays at his office and these give him an option he can accept!

Personally, I LOVE them on him!! They look so nice and flattering!  He doesn't have much in the hind area, and these manage to disguise that a bit and accentuate his muscular thighs...and they look very trimming.

In addition to the soft, stretchy material, the hardware and detail on the jeans is absolutely top-notch!  Stitching is smooth and even and the seams are nice and secure.  The hems are extremely subtle, which adds to a little bit of a dressier feel to the jeans.  (Not the usual bulky hem that most of his jeans feature.)  The material is 98% cotton and only 2% spandex, but it is enough to really give them a gentle elastic quality.

My husband has lost some weight, so I was guessing a 32 might fit him, but these are actually a little more generous in the waistline than we had expected.  He is not one to be caught without a belt (ha ha), so no worries for him, but this pair definitely ran a little large.

We have laundered these inside out in cold water (always use a little vinegar when washing dark colors the first time).  We have laid these flat to dry and then he likes them best when I run our Jiffy Steamer over them (yes...he is quirky!),  Still, they look amazing and fit great!

Things I liked: The main characters were endearing and had good hearts. The settings were interesting and I really wanted to love the story, but...
Things I didn't like:I couldn't feel the emotion. There were many things to feel in this book like the loss of a beloved mother and falling in love, but I couldn't feel it. It all just happened as a matter of course. Especially the falling in love. After his mother told him he was then he realized he was and he told her so. Then she said she was too. It just fell flat for me. He thought she was pretty, she thought he was handsome, but I didn't see the love coming in their thoughts or their actions. Even when they kissed it was like, "that was really nice." I don't like explicit sex, but I do like to at least feel their attraction and desire. It just wasn't there.

This was a quick read in both a good and bad way.  The conflict could have been drawn out instead of feeling almost like a side note.  It kept the pace fast though while still inspiring emotional investment.  I simply wantedmore: more of the characters, both main and support, and more from the romance (such as seeing the vision come true).  You can tell this wasn't the first book in the series, but it doesnt much matter.  I am interested in the others though.

The characters were very compelling.  They were fun and down to Earth.  As a unit, they complimented each other well.  I just wish we could have seen more of their bonding on screen, but that again would have slowed the pace of the book down.  Im hoping to see more of them and explore other characters from their groups (falcons and lions) in future books!

A Promise on White Wings was a short and sweet read with some yummy scenes and an interesting world.  Dont miss this one!

I liked this book and all, but I do have a few mixed feelings about it.  I like Tony by the end, but never particularly fell in love with him.  He was frequently pretty asinine.  Frances, however, I loved.  She gave in to Tony a little more than I wouldve liked, but their romance wouldnt have progressed if she hadnt, and they ended in a good place.  Shes pretty much a badass and I loved all the scenes where she got to showcase that!  Her history of survival really resonated with me and I appreciated that part of her past and how it shaped her.

This book stands alone just as well, maybe even better than the last.  The couples from the first two books are there and everything, but this really was very much about Tony and Frances alone.  The story is good, though a little slow at times.  I will say that one thing bothered me: theres a no-protection love scene and they make kind of a big deal about it, but then protection is never mentioned again.

Overall, I think they compliment each other pretty well and they're very sweet and sexy, but Tony himself is just a little too rough around the edges for me to really adore them, but I think thats just me.

He's evoking feelings she hasn't felt in a long time, and she feels slightly indebted to him for saving her life... she also doesn't trust him, or anyone for that matter. Her hero, Sloane, gets what he wants... and he will get her.

I think the NY Times has lost credibility with the alarmingly good review of this scattered, confusing mess and utterly boring film!  As usual Tom Wilkinson and Paul Giamantti were exceptional, Clive Owens believable and sexy, but Julia Roberts was as uncharismatic as I've ever seen her, looking haggard throughout the film, mouthing off like an unhappy 12 year old as she usually does in place of actually acting, flat, bland love scenes with about as much appeal as a bowl of cold oatmeal, a spy story that was so convoluted you had no idea of what was happening, and you wonder just how anyone could praise this film!

I had high expectations awaiting the arrival of the DVD
"The Lovely Bones", and all I can honestly say, it had to be the worst film I've seen in years.  Flat, empty cardboard type characters, a meandering script that had so much fantasy you thought you were watching a bad cartoon, overdone and all over the place, I had no idea of what I was watching.

Stanley Tucci was great though, and brought a real creepy presence which gave the film some grit which it very much needed.

This book fell flat for me. Aubree seemed to mature unrealistically fast. She ran from what happened to her for almost a year, which continued after she came home, and then one trip back to 'the scene of the crime' and she can deal. Booker was just as bad. It just seems like they blow things out of proportion, which I understand is a teenage thing to do, but then all of a sudden they don't. Also, Booker having released more than one best selling books on his own in nine months is crazy in itself, but to have also invested in both of his brothers and built himself and his mother a house in that time is even more crazy.
Overall, this was kind of a bore. All of the suspense the author tried to create throughout the book was easy to figure out. The story ended up being more about how long it was going to take the characters to figure it out, which wasn't all that entertaining.
I will admit when I realized Ben was not finding a new love, but his wife I thought Shayne was taking the easy way out. I was pleasantly surprised by this story. I think this was my favorite one yet.

I really have no problem with Christian romance, but this one was a little too preachy for me. I guess some of my problem has to do with the authors idea of what it means to be a Christian. There were a couple of times were the implication was made that regular trips to church is one thing that makes a person a Christian. I think it has more to do with beliefs and how you live your life. Also, the relationships between the characters were lacking. It seemed Alec's marriage proposal was based solely on their past relationship because there was really no new relationship developed.

Sweet romance between two people who are polar opposites. Some of the writing is a little cliche, but it is a good story. I enjoyed seeing how tables would turn and secrets would be revealed. Definitely recommend.

It was entertaining to watch Abigail, on her expedition for revenge, fall into so many compromising positions.  When I wasn't feeling sorry for her, I wanted to shake some sense into her.  The tension between her and Nicolas could have been cut with a knife, and their run-ins became almost comical.  There were moments I laughed, moments I gasped and moments I shed a tear or two.  It was very well written and very romantic.  Thank you for a wonderful read.

This docking-system-slash-alarm-clock has some amazing features. Dual alarms that can be set up to go off only on certain days? OMG where have you been all my life!?! But I didn't pick this out for that. No, I wanted it as a place to dock/charge my iPad 2 at my bedside so I could cut back on the sea of cords I have there.

Unfortunately after the first couple of uses I decided this dock doesn't offer enough support or stability for the iPad 2. The plastic holder doesn't even properly rest against (they literally do not touch one another at all) the back of my iPad 2. The charging port doesn't sit flush enough with the actual dock when in place that I felt comfortable leaving it there. In short, it charged to perfection but I didn't feel comfortable leaving it there for more than a night. It looked like it was ready to fall off and considering the cost of replacing my iPad 2 should it have fallen... it just wasn't worth the risk to me.

Now... as far as everything else goes I love this product. The sleek design is very attractive. The sound quality is stellar, but I wouldn't have expected anything less from Philips. The controls can take some getting used to, be sure and save your instructions booklet at your bedside until you get the hang of it. I've never had a remote for an alarm clock before and to be honest haven't cared to use it other than when I played around with the iPod app on my iPad. If you're looking for an iPhone or iPod Touch docking station and alarm I really think this would be one of exceptional quality. It would definitely have better support for these smaller (not to mention lighter) devices than it did for my iPad 2. Maybe it worked better with the first iPad?

Overall this didn't work out for my needs as I had hoped but I've been thinking of adding an iPod to my gadget collection so hopefully I'll get some use out of that pairing. Other than not thinking it's well paired with the iPad 2 I really like this product and would recommend it to smaller gadget users looking for a docking alarm.

We got this ship a couple of days ago, and my almost-5-year-old munchkin -- my granddaughter -- absolutely loves it.

It's the perfect size for her to play with the enclosed Playmobil pirates (very similar to Lego), who apparently are perfect suitors for her little Barbies and Disney princesses. The whole gang piles on board to sail off to their group "wedding", which usually takes place at one of her princess castles or Barbie Dream Houses.

I find this toy to be pretty impressive. It's not some dinky toy boat; this thing is pretty big, with plenty of room for her to move the figurines around so she can actually have them do things on board, as opposed to other toy ships on which you can only place the figures and not have them do much for lack of space.

It's really detailed, right down to the binnacle compass.

It was very easy to assemble, taking only about 10 minutes or so. The instructions -- consisting of pictograms -- were easy to understand and follow, with only one exception: be advised that the treasure chest isn't mentioned for some reason. I kept trying to pry the darned thing open, to the point of almost breaking it. FYI, it turns out that if you slide the keyhole escutcheon to the side, the chest unlocks and opens. I'll also publicly admit that it was the MUNCHKIN, not me, who actually figured this out (all that wasted time and money studying engineering in college... go figure).

it's very sturdy and I'm sure will stand up to a lot of abuse. Be aware that there are quite a few small parts that I expect will ultimately get lost, at least some of them: swords, knives, a flintlock pistol, hats, pirate booty consisting of individual tiny gold coins. I'd suggest storing the stuff in  the lockable chest or the enclosed barrels, but let's face it: kids will be kids, and at least some of this stuff is going to "vanish".

Overall, I'd consider this a job extremely well done by Playmobil. Terrific toy worth every penny of its price.

Unfortunately, nowhere on the Amazon Product Page or description is that limitation mentioned. In fact, the blurb states that "Guardzilla is an all in one home security system". This book was a strong three stars for me. There were things about it that were wonderful and things I thought got overlooked. It easily drew me in with just the blurb and that hot cover. Once I started the book I was hooked. The characters were well written and relatable. The storyline was interesting and though not entirely original there were aspects of the story that helped it stand out from similar books.

Laney is strong, sassy, opinionated, and seems to attract men who aren't worthy of her. Until she catches the eye of Heath who just moved in down the hall. But he runs so hot and cold it's hard to tell what he's thinking most of the time. Heath isn't looking for a relationship but something about Laney grabs his attention and won't let go. She may just be another complication in his life or she may be the answer to all his problems.

If you like books where the guy is kind of a jerk and the girl doesn't instantly swoon you'll like this book. Both characters have big personalities that both clash with and compliment each other. While the sex scenes are hot and fun I feel like they out weighed the actual storyline. I found myself needing more, their story was full of twist, turns, and deceit but, a lot of that went to the wayside once they gave into their need for each other. I would have liked to see this book delve into more of the dark and drama, see it played out more, and have it be about more than just their relationship.

All in all a strong book that I enjoyed from start to finish.

Kye was amazing! He was the perfect mix of alpha and sweet. He wasn't afraid to do what he needed to do to prove how he felt. He understood what was going on and had the patients to see it through.

The storyline and writing were great like all the other books in this series. The cover is hot and really what drew me to the book in the first place. An overall good read.

I love owls and I will use these placemats all year long and not just on Thanksgiving. These placemats are 100% polyester and measure 13"x19". The owls and oak tree design are embroidered on rather than printed. The placemats are dark brown and the embroidered design is white. Because of the embroidery, these placemats should be gently hand washed in cold water and hung to dry. Very pretty placemats.

These are nice 100% cotton placemats. They look nice on a country table or a more dressed up classy table. But once you have to wash them, that's where the disappointment comes in. I wouldn't wash them in the washing machine if I were you. Even though it says they can be washed in the machine, they will come out warped and never in the same shape again. Your best bet would be to hand wash them, and even then you're not guaranteed that they will still be in the same shape as they were before you washed them. They are heavy and not easy to wash by hand. You might be able to get away with hanging them on the line and spraying them with a hose and then laying them flat to dry.
If you do throw them in the washing machine, you'd best make sure you don't throw them in with anything you don't want to dye. Especially the red ones. They bleed terribly. I'd test the dye before you wash with anything else. I'm guessing blues and purples are going to bleed pretty badly as well.

If you want to work hard to keep these looking as good after washing as they do when you first get them, then these aren't bad. I wouldn't buy these again.

I bought this nice looking pan from the "Product Dimensions discription" that Amazon shows here. Which is: 14.5 X 11.8. I thought this was going to be a big Oval pan, with a high dome lid that is shown..The lid is not so high dome, but is very usable and nice.
 So I'm very disapointed that it is a round 12 inch pan that it does say at the top of the page....

 When I called Amazon, they told me it was the big oval pan size!

 I wish someone would have given a review on the measurments, and Amazon would have known the truth!!!

 I have used this pan one time. For me it seemed too shallow , which means food is going to spill out onto my stove top..
 The side Handles got too hot, and I had my burner on the low side.
 I let this pan cool down before I started to wash it, and right away the inside turned colors on the bottom of the pan! I don't know if that happened cause I cooked with Wine.
 The only thing that would take this out was Bar Keepers Friend.thank goodness!

 I also bought at the same time a Farberware stainless 5 quart oval cassarole. I have to say, the Farberware handles do not heat up on the stove top, the inside does not turn different colors when washed, and it heats more even.
 I always thought Cuisinart would be a higher grade cookware then Farberware, but not in this case..

 98% of my other cookware is Calphalon Commercial,and the Farberware cooks almost as good, but not the Cuisinart !

  I'm disapointed in this pan the way it cooked, the deepth,the HoT handles, and the way it cleaned, till I used the bar keepers friend, which is a must to have for Stainless and copper.

 I think this pan for me will be used to put food in after its been cooked, because this looks nice to serve in for a buffet.
 Just for the looks, I'm giving this a 3 star.

This is a cute little alphabet book for young children, consisting of made-up animals.  The illustrations are cute, if a bit primitive, but the descriptions aren't always going to be interesting enough for the target audience of children learning the alphabet.

Casual sex can be a joyful and thrilling part of life, but this short teaser made it seem creepy and soul-deadening. Our heroine locks eyes with a man she will dub "Mr. Tongue," a weird bit of depersonalization that I guess is okay because "Sex in the City," and they meet in a closet for a quick bout of oral sex. His tongue, we're told, is like a penis in length and thickness, an image I found more disturbing than arousing. Were they even human? We're told that she bites his shoulder to stifle her screams . . . while he is still engaged in giving her oral. What? How?

Physically how did this work?

After witnessing the wedding, they reunite in his hotel room. They couple in a curiously impersonal way: no names are exchanged, there is little joy or affection. Her preference, I think, would be for him not to exist outside of her need for sexual gratification. This certainly explains her dismay when she encounters him later. The nerve of him, to continue existing after she got finished with him! He is pleasant, although also engaged to her sister. She is churlish and rude. Was he supposed to dissolve into a puff of smoke after she got off?

There is something so sad about this story. Watching these two find love isn't something I would look forward to.

Fighting may be the author's passion or it may just be the passion he decided to give his character, but it wasn't really enough to carry the entire book for me.

Josiah is a young MMA fighter who, mid-training run, stumbles into the hidden world of vampires -- oh, I'm sorry -- "mani" that surrounds him. He is quickly sucked into their orbit. The love story seemed a bit tangential to the story and most of the plot is conveyed during a pillow talk info dump towards the end of the book, making it difficult for me to care.

The book isn't the worst written self-published paranormal out there, but there is certainly some room for improvement.

Overall, the author's world isn't really one that appeals to me that much. The details about the carni and the mani and the triat just seemed obviously contrived, as did the ending.

I found this short romance unbelievable and dull.

I'm not sure how the two main characters fell in love.  They only knew each other four days and they hardly spent any time together.  Attraction I can understand.  Love just didn't make any sense.

Unbelievable can be overcome in a romance, but this was just very dull too.  The characters were just so good - unrealistically, relentlessly, unceasingly good - and nothing much of interest happens to them.

Maybe if this had been a full length novel the author could have made the love story more convincing, the characters more than one-dimensional, and inserted some action or real conflict.  There was conflict, but the resolutions were telegraphed so explicitly to the reader that you never feel the impact of it.

Works great and takes great video with my canon 5D III.
Very very fast.

I have spent so much on professional photography for my daughter, and although I consider myself a hobbyist photographer, I never thought I could get the same quality. I used a Nikon D90 for a while, and my pictures were nice, but didn't have the same WOW factor that I got with my professionally shot photos.

Since I started using my 5D Mark III, my pictures are in a different ballpark. It's way too simplistic to say that the camera makes the picture ... because a great photographer can take amazing shots with an iPhone ... lighting, framing ... lots more to a shot than the camera.

But I will say that with the 5D in my hands I haven't taken a bad shot. I've done some sessions for friends, and through word of mouth I've gotten inquiries for some paid shoots and have done a few (so I guess I'm borderline past hobbyist).

Also, the low light performance is INSANE. I get clear sharp shots in dimly lit rooms without a flash. Took some family shots in a restaurant for my daughter's birthday, and they're perfect ... even with low lighting.

Love this camera in every way. And the kit lens is really well past what you expect from a kit lens.

Both Anna and Ethan have a lot of baggage, and much of this story is how they two of them learn to cope, overcome, and become better people despite their pasts.

I related to Anna mostly.  Both of us come from an abusive relationship, and many of her struggles are ones I've been through myself.  There were times I felt like I was actually watching clips from my past.

There's a lot of laughs, a good deal of intensity, many bits of sexy-times, and a few "WTF?!?!?!?!" moments.  I love a book that gives me a broad range of emotions.

My issues with this book were mostly editing related.  I felt it needed some work.  It's not bad, but it is noticeable.  Also, there were a few parts that seemed a little rushed and not fully explained.  An example of this would be the entirety of the character Sarah.

Mostly though, I enjoyed reading it.  It's a powerful love story about overcoming past hardships with Doctor Who references!

First of all, I'm already a fan of Cassie Mae, so I was excited when this book was released.

One thing that needs to be pointed out, there's a lot of references to the show How I Met Your Mother.  I have never seen it, so I didn't understand any of those bits.

The story itself was amusing, and I laughed a lot.  There were a few times I clinched my chest because my heart was hurting.  Mostly though, it felt a little too cheesy. I'm not saying I disliked Jace and Shay because they were adorable.  It just felt a bit too forced.

Sadly to say, I was disappointed within the first bit of the book.  Finding out the female love interest is Korean, but the girl on the cover is absolutely not any flavor of Asian was upsetting.  I recognize that this is the fault of Random House, and I was offended they would white wash the cover.  That they would do this to an author I'm quite fond of felt like a betrayal to me.

One thing I really did like was how the subject of Jace's dyslexia was handled.  It's a topic that I don't feel is addressed enough, and I think it was awesome of Cassie Mae to show how someone can succeed even with those struggles.  I was also impressed with how Shay approached it.

There's a character in here, Milo, he's awesome.  I kinda wished there was more about him.  He's probably my favorite.

All and all, the story was cute and I did enjoy it.  I disliked the cover choice, because Random House is lying to the potential readers.  And I thought the characters were pretty darn spiffy.

Not our favorite treats for the mutts. Rawhide, in general, is not the best treat for dogs.

Rawhide treats come from the inner layer of cow or horse hides. During manufacturing, the hides are cleaned and cut or ground. Then they're pressed into chewable dog treats of different shapes and sizes. To make them more appealing for dogs, some rawhide treats contain beef, chicken, or liver flavorings.

The main risks in giving your mutts rawhide is contamination, digestive irritation, choking or blockages.

I only gave my canine testing team 1 treat each. The big mutts, Kali and Kona, chewed them pretty darn fast. Our little mutt, Chewie, took his time, but did not like the chicken wrap.

Made in Cambodia.

Please wear gloves and eye protection. Keep kids, pets, and wives inside.

This is an attractive and very tidy set of scales. Measuring just 7 inches by 7 inches, the tempered glass platform is very easy to keep clean. Operation is simple by using two switches on the front, one of which turns the scales on or off or zeros them and the other switches between units.

Measurements available are pounds and ounces, grams or milliliters. It is easy to switch between these measures and the scales default to the last unit used when they are switched on again. The maximum capacity of the scale is 11 pounds or 5 kilograms, which is plenty for most normal uses. A useful feature is that it turns itself off when it has not been used for a little while to conserve the battery which is a lithium CR2032 supplied with the unit. These batteries last for ages, cost literally cents to replace and are available on Amazon. The battery access panel easily clips off - no screws to mess around with. You can also turn off the scales manually. It has a useful tare feature whereby you can put an empty vessel on the scales and then set it to zero by pressing the left hand switch. Having added the first ingredient in the required quantity you can again switch it to zero with just a click and so on.

These scales are very easy to use and the display can be easily read from any angle. The unit appears to be well constructed and the price is very competitive. It comes complete with a magnetic conversion table to show the conversion of cups into fluid ounces into tablespoons into milliliters. The manufacturers kindly sent me a sample of this item so that I could write an objective review.

This is a safe and effective rat bait station.  I have had a mouse problem in my home before and I found that other Tomcat products were effective, so I decided to try this for the outside areas.  I have a deck in the back of my home that was my first spot to try this.  I put it under the edge and the very next day there was a mouse inside.  It was still alive, so I left it alone.  I loved having the convenience of the clear top for that.  I haven't found any dead mice or rats close to my home, but I have seen where something has eaten the poison.  I will continue to use the Motomco Tomcat stations.

I have three dogs.  Two cocker spaniels and a jack russell terrier.  Unfortunately none of them gets the proper amount of exercise, so I keep them on Costco's Kirkland's Weight Management food.  They like the taste of it and it does keep their weight steady.  I wanted them to try something different to see if any of them would actually loose weight.  They have only been eating this for a month.  None of them has lost weight, but it might take longer for any results.  Two of my dogs instantly liked the flavor and wanted to eat it immediately, but one dog took a while before he would eat it.  From the beginning, this gave one dog gas, one dog threw up a couple of times and all of them have very foul smelling stools.  None of them got constipated.  I did gradually introduce it to them, so I was surprised at the immediate reactions.  In the end two of the dogs get gas and their stools are still way more foul than they were before, so I decided to stick with the Kirkland's brand.

A nice young woman with a selfish and unloving father tries to find some happiness in spite of a jealous and nasty older sister.
This author has a gift for sucking you in and tricking you into thinking you know what is happening. I liked this book.
The story was okay but why ruin it with sex? Can't an author think of better things to write about than stuff that is private?
This story has interesting characters and the plot was fun to guess at and the writing was clear. A good, clean mystery.
What happened? I settled in to read this book and it was way too short!  I want more . I don't want to wait for more.

I had a hard time reading this one. Laddie got on my last nerve from the beginning.  I also had a hard time with the narration. Sometimes it was first person and then the next paragraph wad in third person. Very odd writing style.

I was really looking forward to reading this one, but it fell short for me.  We get a glimpse into Elle's feelings for Adam but only to certain pieces through diary entries.  Really short story that basically retold snippets from On Dumlin Street.

3.5 stars

Fearless is Hunter's story and it takes place before Storm. So you could even read this before you read Storm. I liked this story, it gave me some insight in Hunter's character. Really enjoying this sseries so far

My husband, for Christmas, asked for a "Dressier Sweatshirt".  He wears plain old sweatshirts around the house in the winter.  They're comfy and warm.  But if we're going to visit the grandkids and he's going to be outside, a "dressier" sweatshirt looks better.  So, of course, I didn't hesitate to order this navy Carhartt Crew Neck Sweatshirt.
He liked it and has already worn it.  After washing, it looks good as new.
Heavy fabric, well made.  Color is exactly as pictured
I gave this four stars because it was a good story. It was interesting but  main female  character was  strong but yet acted out of character 're her family.

Though I was a bit confused for a time while reading this book, eventually things became clear and I was left with the thought:  Oh! clever!  I see what you did there.

It was a quick read, and enjoyable.

Brett is a billionaire who meets teen mother Laurie in the park one day.  If this sounds improbable, I'd agree.  The rest of the book is full of more improbable events, and I have to say I LOVED it.  Brett is a character who is so over the top crazy about Laurie and her kids that he has no problem letting his obsession with them show to any and all who care to look.  He is protective of them to the extreme.  He is jealous, controlling and pushy.  But he says the sweetest things to Laurie, and treats her like a precious gem, that I couldn't help but overlook his cave-man antics.  (I honestly think the author wrote Brett's character with total tongue in cheek.)

If you're a serious feminist you will hate this book.  But then again, you wouldn't be looking for anything in this genre anyway. :)  For anyone else, the book is a quick read full of hilarious comments from the MC, Brett.  Examples:

" We're just going to take things nice and slow until you get your bearings, and then we'll do things my way."

"Babe, I have an appointment, can you have this meltdown when I get back?"  [wow, patronizing much?]

This book is full of little gems from this guy.  Laurie is just swept up in his vortex of cocooning emotions.  Lucky Laurie!

The book started out with a great premise.  Hire a PI to see if the boyfriend is cheating on you.  Great start to a plot.  And I thought it was going to be good.  But the further I got into the book, the more ridiculous main character Milo became.  1) He was OBSESSED with Dusty's coat.  I get it.  It's hot.  I can picture it.  But good grief, stop talking about the coat.  2) He pitches a fit over his ex taking the TV when he moved from the house.  Then admits, "Well, he did buy it."  uh......okay.  3) He talks in a ridiculously cliched way.  "Give it to me, big boy."  Seriously, who talks like that unless they are joking!  4) He is not very smart when he is confronted by his ex.  He basically spills his guts out of pride and temper, rather than show himself to be clever and outsmart the ex.  Guess he needed to have that melodramatic rescue by the new boyfriend.  (Oh, after multiple sexual encounters and moving in together, THEN they decide to MAYBE, PERHAPS accept the label of boyfriend. )

Now, since the book started with promise and the second book in the series is on my Kindle already, I think I'll read it.  I hope it's better.  (I am disappointed, though, to see that the book does not involve Milo's brother.  Nor does book 3 involve one of Dusty's 'no good' brothers, which I thought might have been a neat way to redeem at least one of them, but....

By the end I really liked these two and to be honest, the epilogue was the best!  Throughout the story, I kept getting distracted by two things:  referring to male anatomy as a 'member.'  Ummm, 1973 called and they want their erotic terminology back. :)  The other thing I was bugged by was Jake acting like he was 40+.  I get that it's a physical job.  Tough work.  Be he's not even 30.

Okay, beyond that, Jake and Ethan together are really cute.  Their time sitting by the pond and fishing is really sweet.  Ethan's discovery that he needs to permanently get rid of his 'off-on-off' girlfriend is telling about his character.  He's no cheater.  I like that in a MC.
The oh reason one star appears is because I don't know how to get them to brighten.  Good story and rapid read.  Am getting used to all the typos.
This book was very difficult to follow and get a feeling of understanding.  It was not funny or serious.  Just a poorly designed story with no real depth to it.  Not one I would recommend.

The Miracle-Gro AeroGarden Sprout was welcomed with open arms at our house.  We used the larger version of this indoor planter last year with great success, and this one also looks good to go.

The Miracle-Gro planters are simple to set up and use.  The instructions are clear (not something we take for granted any longer), and the concept is simple.

The plants grow in water, with plant food and fresh water provided every two weeks.  Light comes from the overhead adjustable lamp for sixteen hours a day; the time of day the light is on can be programed into the system.

We had great success with our indoor herb garden last year and actually ordered additional seed pods to continue into spring.  There's a fairly large variety of herbs offered when ordering replacement pods.  (Frankly the included dill is easy to grow, but requires constant trimming to keep it from overwhelming the other plants.)

On a personal note, I find the sound of the motor to be loud and we therefore keep our unit in a little used room.  I would find it distracting in a kitchen, office, or studio apartment, but others may differ.

The LED Grow Light is predicted to last 6 months.  Last winter's bulb was a different type and burned out within the first month; it was replaced at no cost to us.  We are not anticipating problems with this one.

All in all, we're looking forward to fresh basil on Christmas Day.

The T-fal Hot Air Popcorn Popper does an adequate job but it's far from the popper of my dreams.  For quick perusal here are the major pros and cons:

Pros:
It's attractive enough to sit out on the kitchen counter.  The black plastic hood and stainless steel base fit in well in many kitchens.
And the small footprint makes it easy to store.
It has a power switch.
The top section can be washed in the dishwasher.
And it has a built in butter melter and a measuring spoon.

Cons:
While in use, the unit gets quite hot.
The lack of height makes it difficult to place a large bowl under the hood to catch the flying kernels. And they do fly.
And most importantly, there's a higher percentage of unpopped kernels than with our older Presto model.

Air popped corn seems to taste the same from all poppers.  And all the poppers we've tried do leave some kernels unpopped.  So this is pretty much a standard air popper; for us the heat of the unit is the major disadvantage.

But potential buyers might want to check out the Presto popper reviews before they make a final decision.
You definitely caught my attention but why such a short excerpt?? Totally need to hear more about Lucien Lucien again why just a tease!!!
Loved the characters and story immensely. I enjoyed your characters : The Rhea and Chad . I appreciate all the service men and women!! My son-in-law is currently stationed in Okinawa, Japan.
This was a wonderful short story, featuring two of my favorite characters, in what has become one of my favorite series, and I wish that this one had been a little longer.

I remember when this came out, back and 2012, I couldn't wait for it to be released on DVD/Blu-Ray, so I could watch it (I don't have cable). When it arrived last week I immediately put it in to watch and it's stayed there in my player off and on ever since. Very well done, and well acted. I found myself thoroughly caught up in the story. It is well worth the time to watch. I've actually done some reading about the real events, suffice it to say that this is a very dark and tragic story.

I thought it was a strange phenomenon when I kept finding a line of ants crawling in an arc across the pantry door in my kitchen.  My roommate, Bill, said they were grease ants.  I had never heard of grease ants.  He told me to rub vinegar on them.  The vinegar would kill the tiny black insects but they would reappear--marching across the pantry door in a perfect arc.  Finally, I tried the Hot Shot Ultra Liquid Ant Bait.

  I set out all four bait stations and easily opened them.  Within a few days, I noticed ant corpses in and around the stations.  After a couple of weeks, all the ants were gone.  They never reappeared.  Some of the insects must have taken the poisoned liquid to the nest and the queen subsequently died.  The Hot Shot Ultra Liquid Ant Bait is easy to use and very affordable.  Furthermore, because the bait stations are transparent, I know when it is time to buy new ones.

"Hell Night" stars adorable, vivacious Linda Blair of "Exorcist" fame.  She must spend the night in the abandoned, decrepit Garth manor along with three other sorority and fraternity pledges.  Members of Sigma Phi Rho have rigged the house to emit spooky sounds and images.  Unknown to them all, Garth Manor is not as abandoned as it appears.  A deranged mongoloid remains and is determined to kill all intruders using a number of gruesome weapons.  Who will survive this night of hell?

  This slasher flick from the eighties is great to watch on Halloween or on any stormy night.  In fact, the producer, Irwin Yablans, who brought us "Halloween" also co-produced this fright fest.  The gothic Garth manor, huge and creepy, is the perfect setting for murder and mayhem.  It is surrounded by a spiked fence with gates that are locked, trapping the pledges within.  The chase scenes within the maze of hedges are accentuated by suspenseful music; they reminded me of Elke Sommer being pursued in Mario Bava's "Baron Blood."

  Good performances are given by all, especially Blair.  Vincent Van Patten, however, grew annoying as the wise cracking surfer dude.  I was disappointed that the film didn't have a higher body count since Anchor Bay described it as " . . . an `80s body-count classic."  The ending was shocking and violent.  The last still frame of a stunned Blair slowly walking away from the manor was memorable.

  "Hell Night" is worth seeking out if you enjoy good slasher fare such as "Halloween," "The Last House on Sorority Row," "Prom Night," and "Terror Train."  Watching this movie will make you think twice about trespassing on someone else's property at night.

I've read other books by Joshua Graham, so I picked this one up just because of his name. This one was not nearly as good as the others. The setting was unclear, and the characters were sketchy. The author delved into the story without giving enough background info. I didn't even make it halfway through.

Raymond is down to his final day on death row. His mother and brothers travel to the prison to visit him one last time.

This is quite a different story for Grisham. He's a great novelist, but his short stories are just as good. The ending of the story caught me by surprise, but I guess as a lawyer, Grisham has seen the good and the bad and tells both sides.

BANG BANG introduces readers to Axton and Amy. Forced away as a child, Amy is living a shattered life until Axton rescues her. He brings her back to Chicago, and then the two learn that they are to marry. Although they're in love, a forced, spur-of-the-moment wedding isn't what they had planned. The novel easily flows into the next in the series.

This novel was okay. The characters just didn't have the charisma of some of her other characters. The story was too short to develop the characters, leaving the reader wanting a bit more. All together, I enjoyed this novel. I just wish it had been longer.
SHE DOES KNOW JACK has a good plot, but I thought the characters were a bit lacking. The novel jumped right into the action without giving much background about the characters.

I hate to write bad reviews. After an author works hard to write a novel, I feel he deserves credit for at least that. But this? My head was spinning when I got to the end. (I have to admit that I read about 45% before I skimmed.) If you're into an overdose of hormones and impulsive, reckless sex, then you may enjoy this novel. But if you want a plot with developed characters, keep looking.

Basically, Kyle is a private investigator. Sharon pays him to spy on her husband. Her husband is boring, though. Kyle becomes tired of watching him sit at his computer or eat. Then a young girl walks in. She's cute, hot, and overflowing with hormones. Kyle falls for her immediately. After a chance meeting, Kyle decides it's time to break the ice. Then they have sex. And more sex. And more sex. The story of Kyle's investigation takes a back seat to his lingering teenage hormones.

This novel could have been much better. Instead it was more like a porn movie.
